Completing a run with a SKIPPED stop strands its orders on the happy path, exactly as cancelling does
symptom: updateRunStatus's COMPLETED gate treats SKIPPED as done (routes.service.ts:1424 filters s.status !== COMPLETED && s.status !== SKIPPED), so a run with a skipped stop completes normally and that stop's orders keep routeRunStopId against a finished run — the same permanent PREVIOUSLY_DISPATCHED strand as B129, but reached with no cancel involved. B129 as filed covers only the CANCELLED branch. F11's B34/B146 make driver-initiated skips reachable for the first time, so this batch INCREASES the frequency of an uncovered strand. Found by the F11 batch synthesis, 2026-09-02.

title: A SKIPPED stop has no reopen or skip control anywhere in the product — a dead-end state, not just a strand
location: apps/mobile/app/(operator)/route-runs/[id].tsx — stop row actions (:461-468); no web stop-reopen caller exists

So B211's stranded orders have no in-product recovery and B146's 'only until a human intervenes' was false. Found by the F11 analysis (Opus A, 2026-09-02). Batch is an OWNER call: the file is co-touched by F11 (B129's cancel button :385+) and F20 (B32 :351/:379) — filed unbatched so it lands in triage.

title: A same-key retry after a failed idempotency-key write re-folds an already-committed buyer merge
symptom: After a committed buyer merge, a failed recordIdempotencyKey call is only logged (orders.controller.ts:207-213), so a client retry with the same idempotency key re-runs the fold and computes ABSOLUTE totals a second time over the same cart -- the same swallowed-money-failure class as B58 (F18 sibling-sweep finding, 2026-09-06). A complete fix collides with the standing rule that customer merges serialize through withAdvisoryLock with no transaction threaded into updateOrderItems; recorded in F18's result.json as a deferred owner question (is the accepted failure still acceptable, should recordIdempotencyKey move inside the merge transaction, or should the merge fail closed when the record cannot be written), not fixed by F18.

title: Reinstating a lapsed tenant does not clear a downgrade armed before the lapse
symptom: F18 made onSubscriptionDeleted/onSubscriptionUpdated clear downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt/retainedUserIds, matching the one-armed-transition invariant subscription-mutation.service.ts now documents, but onPaymentSucceeded and onCheckoutCompleted (the reinstatement webhooks) do not: a tenant that lapses with a downgrade already armed keeps that stale schedule through reinstatement, so the next 02:00 sweep re-prices basePriceSnapshot against the pre-lapse schedule, books a second MRR delta, and can deactivate staff the reinstatement just restored. A safe fix needs the subscription's prior status available inside the same webhook transaction (F18 Option-B residual, not fixed).

title: A scheduled downgrade deactivates every seat over cap with no way to choose which ones
symptom: F18 ships a server-computed seat warning (seatAckRequired) and a checkbox acknowledgement before committing a downgrade that would exceed the target plan's seat cap, but the sweep itself always writes retainedUserIds: [] -- every OPERATOR/DRIVER over the cap is deactivated with no way for the tenant to choose who stays. A retained-seat picker is the deferred build (owner tradeoff, feature-shaped per campaign DECISIONS.md D5).

title: subscribe() on an off-catalog published plan key writes currentPlan as the STARTER enum shadow
symptom: A fresh subscribe() to a plan key that is not in the published catalog (a catalog-publishing error, not a client bug) falls through planKeyToEnum's else branch and writes Tenant.plan / TenantSubscription.currentPlan as STARTER -- silently misrepresenting the tenant's plan on every screen that reads the enum shadow -- instead of refusing the write. planChangePreview's ACTIVE-tenant path and downgrade() already refuse an unranked/off-catalog key; the fresh-subscribe path does not (F18 sibling-sweep finding, not fixed).

title: A failed re-quote on choose-plan clears the summary card with no error toast
symptom: quote.mutate's onError handler calls clearPreview(), wiping the plan-change summary card with no toast or inline message -- fail-closed by design (a stale preview must not be committable), but the tenant sees the card silently vanish with no explanation. UX copy for the failure state is owed (F18 sibling-sweep finding, not fixed).

title: A post-delivery return on a partly-delivered order cannot separate billed-but-undelivered units from billed-and-delivered ones (deliveredQty composition dropped from F08)
symptom: F08's billed-basis refund (B53) prices every return from the order's creditable invoice items, but a return on an order that was only PARTIALLY delivered and invoiced on the delivered basis has no way to know how much of the billed qty was actually delivered vs still owed -- a correct fix needs a nullable ReturnItem.deliveredQty column (schema migration) persisted in create() and consumed by billedBasisFor: refundQty = deliveredQty != null ? min(returnedQty, max(0, billedQty - deliveredQty)) : min(returnedQty, billedQty). This composition (cause-ruling.md S2 Amendment 2, B53xB128) was dropped from #645 by lead ruling -- no schema change in that wave -- and is owed as its own migration-bearing PR. The 'derive it from OrderItem.deliveredQty instead of a new column' shortcut is REJECTED: OrderItem.deliveredQty is written only by completeStop/completeWithPayment and is not scoped per return, so deriving from it would zero every post-delivery return on a delivered-basis invoice, including ones that never had this bug.

title: GET /returns is role-allowed to DRIVER but findAllForUser scopes only CUSTOMER, handing a driver the tenant-wide return list now priced with refundEstimate money
symptom: The findAll endpoint's @Roles list is (OPERATOR, DRIVER, CUSTOMER), but findAllForUser only special-cases user.role === 'CUSTOMER' (scoping to that customer's own returns); every other role, DRIVER included, falls through to the unscoped this.findAll(options) -- the full tenant-wide list. F08's B75 fix now enriches every row of that list with refundEstimate (billed refund money) and, on a resolved return, effectively refund/credit amounts -- so a DRIVER account can already see other customers' billed return values across the whole tenant. This is a pre-existing role/scoping gap (not introduced by F08) that F08's B75 change makes materially worse by adding money to the payload every DRIVER request now receives. Needs a tenancy carve-out: DRIVER should get either a 403 or its own return-relevant scoping, mirroring the CUSTOMER branch.

title: Return mint-time headroom counts OrderCreditNote-linked credit intent while credit-notes.service caps only against the source invoice, so the guard can refuse a refund the mint would actually accept
symptom: F08's B53 2+-creditable-invoice path computes headroom = Sigma(creditable invoice totals) - Sigma(non-VOID credit notes linked to the order) before minting against the LATEST creditable invoice, deliberately counting order-linked credit-note INTENT (OrderCreditNote) broadly so the mint-time guard cannot be tricked into over-refunding. credit-notes.service.create()'s own cumulative over-credit cap, by contrast, is scoped to the single source invoice being minted against. The two aggregates disagree on scope: an order with credit notes linked to OTHER creditable invoices on the same order can make the returns-side headroom check narrower than what create()'s own per-invoice cap would actually allow, so a legitimate refund can be refused by the mint-time guard even though create() would have accepted it. Needs a product ruling on what 'headroom' should mean across an order's credit-note graph before either side is changed.

title: returns.findAll joins each row's full invoice/invoice-item/order-line graph to compute one refundEstimate scalar, and the controller accepts any client-supplied limit with no upper clamp
symptom: F08's B75 fix prices refundEstimate per row via priceReturn, which needs each return's order's non-VOID/non-WRITTEN_OFF invoice items plus order.lineItems -- selected and joined on every findAll call, then stripped back off the wire per row, purely to derive one number. The web returns page already requests limit: 500 for its KPI/summary fetch (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/returns/page.tsx), and returns.controller.ts's @Query('limit') is parsed with +limit and passed straight through with no Math.min clamp -- so a large or malicious limit multiplies an already-expensive per-row join with no ceiling. Per the repo's limit=0 fetch-all sentinel trap (reference_limit0_fetchall_sentinel_trap.md), any tightening here must first grep every limit:0 / limit:500 caller of this endpoint so a clamp does not silently truncate an existing fetch-all/summary caller.

title: campaign-check's freshness guard collapses its ledger pathspec to the repo root under a hook-inherited GIT_DIR, refusing every push made right after a commit regardless of what it touches
location: scripts/campaign-check.mjs freshness guard, invoked by the pre-push hook
symptom: git exports GIT_DIR to every hook it runs (including pre-push); with GIT_DIR set and no matching GIT_WORK_TREE, running 'git -C <statusDir> rev-parse --show-toplevel' from inside the freshness guard returns statusDir itself instead of the repo root, so path.relative(toplevel, statusDir) yields the empty string and the ledger pathspec used to bound the freshness check collapses to '.' -- the guard then judges freshness against HEAD's own commit time instead of the ledger/test files it should be comparing. Reproduced 2026-09-06 23:1xZ in the rf-ocr worktree: a push issued immediately after a commit was refused by the freshness guard even though nothing it touched was stale. Fix: scrub GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_PREFIX from the environment of every git/turbo child process this script (and any script it calls) spawns, plus a regression spec that sets GIT_DIR before invoking the guard and asserts it still resolves the real repo root.

title: ci-freshness-guard-script.spec.ts T1 (REG-E2EGUARD-403) fails under full host load and passes alone
symptom: T1 drives the deploy-triggered E2E freshness guard's own YAML-defined steps under a faked gh CLI and asserts on outputs.run; under full host load (parallel verify runs, an engine session, or a Docker build competing for CPU/IO) the faked gh invocation can be slow enough that outputs.run comes back undefined, failing the assertion, while the same test is reliably green run alone or on an idle machine. This is a timeout/robustness gap in the test's own harness (the YAML-driven runner it shells out to), not in the guard logic itself, which L-058 already covers for correctness.

title: Mobile optimize callers never render the window-violation signal F12 added
symptom: F12 (PR #652) added OptimizeResult.windowViolations/startTime on the API and wired both web dispatch modals to warn + require acknowledge before a late-stop dispatch; mobile's optimize callers (apps/mobile/lib/api/routes.ts useOptimize*, apps/mobile/app/(driver)/route/index.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/trips/new.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/routes/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/app/(operator)/route-runs/[id].tsx) call the same optimize endpoints but never read windowViolations or render a late-stop warning, so a driver can dispatch a known-infeasible route from the app with no signal at all.

title: 34 orphaned hooks in apps/web/lib/api -- a lint guard is wanted
symptom: F12's refutation.md names B29 (a working useUpdateRouteSettings PATCH-route mutation with zero UI callers) as 'one of 34 orphaned hooks repo-wide' found during the F12 hunt; the full enumeration was not carried into this pipeline's evidence files (only the count and B29's own case are recorded). A repo-wide sweep of apps/web/lib/api/*.ts for exported hooks with zero call sites outside their own file/tests -- the same class of check the bug-hunt scan-signatures.mjs already runs for other dead-hook shapes -- would both enumerate the 34 and give CI a standing guard against new ones accumulating silently.

title: An underway run with no caller clock keeps its scheduled clock and appends unassigned stops unchecked
symptom: F12 recorded residual (fix-round-4-result.json recheck verdict 'not-fixed' for 'Round-3 residual [1] -- underway run with no caller clock appends unassigned stops with no window pass'): optimizeRoute's windowClock gate (route-optimization.service.ts, if(windowClock)) is byte-identical to round 3 -- when a run is IN_PROGRESS and the caller passes no clock, the post-solve window pass is skipped, so a stop the ORS branch reports unassigned is appended to the order with windowsChecked:false and never evaluated against the run's actual (stale) scheduled departure. title: Split-invoice -R{i} sibling numbers are never collision-checked; an out-of-band -R1 row wedges split invoicing with a 409
symptom: F16b/B100 cause refutation + engine final pass, 2026-09-08: runCreation (invoices.service.ts:1230-1252) mints one baseNumber via generateInvoiceNumber(db) (:1222, itself B100's diagnosed generator) then derives every sibling as ${baseNumber}-R${i} (:1234) with no existence check of its own before tx.invoice.create (:1235-1250) - it relies entirely on the base number itself being free; a P2002 on the base self-heals (B100's evidence notes the create path's P2002-to-409 retry), but nothing re-checks or retries a specific -R{i} suffix. If any out-of-band row already holds <baseNumber>-R1 (a prior partial run, a manual insert, an import) the base mint can still succeed while the first sibling's create throws unhandled, wedging the whole split-invoice batch with a 409 that a base-number retry cannot clear.

title: NumberingService.reserveNext's collision guard loops per-candidate (no bulk max scan) - costly once wired to a live mint site
symptom: F16b/B100 cause refutation + engine final pass, 2026-09-08: reserveNext's collision-guarded path (numbering.service.ts:196-234) is a read-modify-write loop that calls the caller-supplied exists(candidate) predicate once per candidate number, advancing n and re-checking (capped at 10,000 iterations, :212-222) rather than computing a bulk max in one query. No live mint site wires an exists predicate in yet (the doc comment at :47-51 calls this "a deferred cross-module change"), so today the cost is latent - but B100's history note says F16b will wire this into all five invoice/estimate mint sites, and the collision path is exactly what a lazily-seeded or import-heavy tenant's first live mint will exercise. If the caller's exists predicate itself does a per-candidate table scan (the naive way to answer "does this number exist"), a long collision run repeats that scan up to 10,000 times inside one guarded transaction instead of computing a numeric max once. Recommend backing exists with an indexed exact-match lookup (cheap per call), or seeding nextNumber from a cached/indexed max instead of a pure collision walk, once real volumes hit this path. Note: verified against current code before filing - no function named scanMaxForYear or any regexp_match-based scan exists in this file today; this row describes the real collision-guard mechanism that occupies the same role.

title: Invoice list's invoiceNumber sort field is plain TEXT - INV-<year>-10000 now sorts before …-9999
symptom: F16b/B100 cause refutation + engine final pass, 2026-09-08: the list endpoint's validSortFields map (invoices.service.ts:2873-2882) points the user-facing "invoiceNumber" sort straight at the invoiceNumber column, which schema.prisma types as plain text - the same lexicographic ordering B100 diagnosed as the root cause of the 9999 mint wall now also skews the READ side once F16b's fix lets series pass 10000: "INV-2026-10000" sorts before "INV-2026-9999" ("1" < "9" at the first differing character), so an operator sorting the invoice list by number sees newer five-digit invoices interleaved ahead of older four-digit ones instead of in creation order. Needs either a numeric sort key derived from the suffix or a padded/fixed-width invariant enforced at mint time.

title: Estimate create() has no P2002-to-409 catch on the number mint - a collision with an imported number surfaces as a 500
symptom: F16b/B100 cause refutation + engine final pass, 2026-09-08: nextEstNumber (estimates.service.ts:15-24) is the same findFirst+orderBy-desc+parseInt generator B100 diagnosed (siblings verified in B100's own evidence: "estimates.service.ts:16-25 tenant-scoped but same pad-4 string-sort wall"). title: bugs.mjs's rootDir() fallback is cwd-relative, not REPO_ROOT-anchored - a drifted shell cwd wrote rows into the wrong checkout
symptom: F16b/B100 cause refutation + engine final pass, 2026-09-08: bugs.mjs:111 defines REPO_ROOT = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "..") specifically so path resolution is "independent of cwd" (its own comment, :107-110) - but rootDir() (:117) does not use it: process.env.BUGS_ROOT || ".claude/campaign", a bare relative literal that Node resolves against process.cwd() when it reaches readFileSync/writeFileSync/mkdirSync. CATALOGUE (:118), STATUS_DIR (:119) and BOARD (:123) are all derived from rootDir(), so every file/sync/index/move invocation without an explicit BUGS_ROOT reads and writes wherever the invoking shell happens to be cwd'd, not the repo (or worktree) the script lives in - exactly what wrote registry rows into the root checkout on 2026-09-08 (reverted). REGISTER (:122) and PIPELINE_DIR (:127) share the identical env-override-with-bare-relative-fallback shape. Fix: default rootDir()/REGISTER()/PIPELINE_DIR() off REPO_ROOT the same way :111 already does, or fail loudly when the resolved root's nearest .git does not match REPO_ROOT.

title: Mobile order edit: margin-floor gate and label use different bases (half-cent boundary disagreement)
symptom: needsMarginAck compares the cent-rounded price against priceForMarginFloor (cost / (1 - floor) rounded to the NEAREST cent via roundMoney, packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts ~:253), while the list row's badge and the picker strip's label classify by the exact fraction (computeMarginFraction -> classifyMargin). At the boundary the two can disagree by up to half a cent in either direction, so a line can show 'Below floor' with no ack asked, or be asked for an ack while classified ok. Fix approach: one basis -- needsMarginAck decides via classifyMargin(computeMarginFraction(price, cost, unitsPerBox), floor) evaluating to other than 'ok' (or priceForMarginFloor rounds UP); pin with a pure test at the boundary (cost 7.00, floor 0.15 -> floor price 8.235 rounds to 8.24; price 8.24 vs 8.23). Found by the #675 final pass (fix-round-3-light.md).

title: Invoice import: a later upload can overwrite a fallback-minted INV number it carries as a source number
symptom: The fallback branch mints INV-<year>-#### for source-numberless rows via NumberingService.reserveNext. symptom: The bulk product-delete endpoint accepted an ids array with no size limit or validation.

title: Credit-notes findOne lacked a method-level role guard; DRIVER could read any credit note in the tenant (F10-003)
symptom: A DRIVER role could read any credit note in the tenant via the credit-notes findOne method.

title: Web and mobile Docker builds used npm install --force instead of npm ci (F12-004)
symptom: The web and mobile Dockerfiles installed dependencies with npm install --force rather than a locked npm ci.

title: Production dependency tree contained critical + high CVEs (F12-001)
symptom: The production dependency tree carried critical- and high-severity CVEs at audit time.

title: All three Docker images ran as root (no USER directive) (F12-003)
symptom: All three RouteFlow Docker images (api, web, mobile) ran their containers as root.

title: Raw Prisma/exception messages echoed to client in bulk-import errors arrays (F8-003)
symptom: Bulk-import error arrays echoed raw Prisma/exception messages back to the client, disclosing DB internals.

title: Customers could mutate line items on already-CONFIRMED orders without re-confirmation (F10-002)
symptom: A CUSTOMER editing a CONFIRMED order's items could leave it CONFIRMED with no re-confirmation of the updated pick list.

title: Vendor-bill payment/update accepted unvalidated any body (F10-004)
symptom: The vendor-bill payment and update endpoints accepted an untyped any request body.

title: Invoice tax base for boxed products used un-prorated raw qty, diverging from the box-prorated subtotal (F10-005)
symptom: Invoice tax for a boxed product line was computed from the raw qty instead of the box-prorated line subtotal, over- or under-stating tax.

title: POST /orders discountAmount unclamped, persists a negative order total
location: apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.ts create() ~L2361-2371 — no clamp against subtotal, missing the guard InvoicesService.create already enforces
symptom: POST /orders with discountAmount greater than subtotal (e.g. 1000 on a $20 subtotal) persists an order with a negative total (e.g. -980); GET /orders/{id} confirms it's durable, not just echoed. InvoicesService.create rejects the equivalent invoice-level case with HTTP 400, but OrdersService.create has no such check.

title: POST /estimates accepts unvalidated client-supplied taxAmount/discount, persists arbitrary/negative totals
location: apps/api/src/estimates/estimates.controller.ts create() ~L14 (dto: any, no class-validator DTO) + estimates.service.ts ~L136-138 (tax/discount taken straight from body, no derivation, no sign check, no bound)
symptom: POST /estimates with taxAmount:-100 on a $20-subtotal estimate persists total:-80; taxAmount:9999 persists total:10019; discount:1000 persists total:-980. Independently GET /estimates/{id} confirms each is durable. Estimates convert to invoices via POST /estimates/{id}/convert-to-invoice, copying est.subtotal/est.taxAmount verbatim, so a fabricated total propagates into real AR.

title: Trial tenant cannot cancel — signup writes no TenantSubscription row for cancel() to act on
symptom: Self-service signup for a trial tenant creates no TenantSubscription row; cancel() previously required that row to exist, so a trial or read-only tenant with no row could never cancel in-app. Fixed: cancel() now runs a compare-and-swap directly on Tenant.status (works with or without a row); READ_ONLY calls are an idempotent no-op; a lost CAS re-read as READ_ONLY still succeeds idempotently, re-read as ACTIVE refuses instead of overwriting a paying tenant.

title: READ_ONLY tenant status was invisible in the web UI
location: apps/web (dashboard)/layout.tsx banner slot, new components/ReadOnlyBanner.tsx, providers.tsx, billing page
symptom: A tenant placed READ_ONLY (trial expired, cancelled, etc.) saw no in-app indication anywhere — no banner, no gating on billing actions. Fixed: GET /billing/subscription carries readOnlyReason (cleared by every self-serve/Stripe-webhook ACTIVE write); new ReadOnlyBanner component with a dedicated layout slot; billing page gates End-trial/Cancel/Keep-my-plan by status; providers.tsx surfaces a READ_ONLY toast.

title: In-app cancel never propagated to Stripe
symptom: cancel()/resume() only wrote TenantSubscription.cancelAtPeriodEnd locally — Stripe was never told, so a tenant who cancelled in-app kept being billed by Stripe with no way to notice. Zero prod exposure at fix time (no tenant yet holds stripeSubId). Fixed: cancel()/resume() now propagate cancel_at_period_end to Stripe BEFORE the local transaction commits.

title: READ_ONLY tenant's Stripe cancel used period-end instead of immediate cancellation
symptom: cancel()'s READ_ONLY short-circuit returned before the Stripe propagation block a later round had added below it, so a tenant the cron took READ_ONLY while its stripeSubId was still live kept being invoiced by Stripe, with no self-serve way out (web hides Cancel for READ_ONLY tenants). Fixed: tell Stripe first; for this cohort cancel IMMEDIATELY rather than at period end (lead ruling, owner-confirmed — the cohort already lost service at its last period end, so a period-end cancel bills a period of nothing).

title: resume() could disarm the payment-reinstatement guard without telling Stripe
symptom: The Stripe call in resume() was gated on three conditions while the local write was gated on one, so a READ_ONLY tenant with a live sub skipped Stripe and still cleared cancelAtPeriodEnd — the exact key onPaymentSucceeded reads — and the next paid invoice reinstated them ACTIVE at +1 MRR. Fixed: that combination now refuses.

title: Admin plan change showed no proration and applied both directions instantly
symptom: The admin plan change surfaced no prorated figure and applied changes instantly in BOTH directions, so it could strip a paying tenant's plan mid-cycle with no credit. Fixed: upgrades prorate and stay instant, downgrades schedule at period end like the tenant path, and the change is refused in either direction while a cancellation is armed. Note: the row's original premise (a Stripe-sync gap between admin and tenant paths) was partly wrong — both paths are Stripe-silent, so there was never an admin-vs-tenant Stripe difference; that half is not filed.

title: Admin reactivation must not silently revoke a tenant-chosen downgrade schedule
symptom: An admin reactivating a non-ACTIVE tenant (non-ACTIVE -> ACTIVE) now leaves an armed tenant-chosen downgrade schedule intact and records it in the admin-action audit meta (downgradeLeftArmed, downgradeEffectiveAt) instead of silently clearing it — an admin action must not revoke a state the tenant chose.

title: Pre-fix invoices keep InvoiceItem.taxRate=0 on order-derived lines, mixing 0-rate and real-rate rows in tax reports
location: apps/api/src/tobacco/tobacco-report.service.ts:~213, tobacco.service.ts:~170/211, analytics.service.ts:~167 (report side); invoice adjustment path (data side)
symptom: #725 fixed taxRate storage going forward, but pre-fix invoices keep taxRate=0 on order-derived lines: (a) an adjustment on any invoice created before #725 still zeroes regular tax (the fix is forward-only), and (b) tobacco/excise reports compute tax collected as subtotal*taxRate and will silently mix 0-rate pre-fix rows with real post-fix rows inside one reporting period. Needs an owner-signed backfill (rate derivable as (invoice.taxAmount - sum(categoryTaxAmount)) / invoice.subtotal, or from the linked order) plus a report-side note. No client identifiers.

title: POST payments still accepted against a WRITTEN_OFF invoice on the primary payment path
symptom: recordPayment refuses only VOID invoices; a WRITTEN_OFF invoice still accepts money via the staff payment endpoint. B312 (#719) guarded only bookkeeping.service.ts:179, not this primary path. Repro: record a payment against a WRITTEN_OFF invoice via the staff endpoint -> accepted.

title: Invoice discount/shipping recalc on update() omits categoryTaxAmount
symptom: A shipping-fee edit on a regulated invoice drops the excise (categoryTaxAmount) from the recomputed total -- the recalc only carries regular tax. Pre-existing; made less visible by #725.

title: Raw AdvancePayment UPDATE bypasses the tenant-scoped query proxy
symptom: Raw UPDATE "AdvancePayment" ... WHERE id = $1 has no tenantId predicate, bypassing the tenantTransaction proxy. Not exploitable today (id comes from tenant-scoped reads), but one refactor away from a cross-tenant write. Add the tenant predicate.

title: changeStatus commits DELIVERED/CANCELLED status write before its own stock/settle transaction
symptom: Same class of bug B283 (#726) closed for DRAFT<->PENDING: the DELIVERED and CANCELLED transitions still commit the status write BEFORE their own stock/settle transactions, so a failure between the two leaves a live status with no matching stock movement. Fold each into one transaction like the DRAFT<->PENDING branches now do.

title: READ_ONLY immediate-cancel treats only Stripe status canceled as terminal
symptom: The cancel path treats only status === "canceled" as success, so incomplete_expired and every other terminal Stripe status still falls to the generic branch, throws 503 on every retry, and leaves stripeSubId intact so the tenant can never get out. Fix the whole terminal SET, never one member at a time. Claimed by 03 (W1 lane).

title: Multiple low-priority findings from the F38/F39/billing review rounds
location: various -- see symptom for per-item file:line
symptom: Bundle of six low items, each independently small: (1) split-sibling invoice tax cents drift -- per-line unrounded ratio vs per-group rounding remainder can differ by cents, no test pins it. (2) apps/web/app/(dashboard)/orders/[id]/page.tsx:~2216 duplicates the tax-rate derivation api's effectiveTaxRateFromTotals (apps/api/src/common/tax-rate.ts, #725) inline -- house rule is one implementation in @routeflow/pricing. (3) platform-admin proratedNow uses catalog prices, ignoring priceOverrideMonthly/discount -- display-only figure shown to admins as money. (4) the new DRAFT<->PENDING Serializable transactions (#726) have no retry, unlike the DELIVERED settle's 3-attempt loop. (5) dropping a dead stripeSubId after a confirmed cancel leaves the id only in a log line; consider a stripeSubIdCancelled audit field. (6) LEGACY_ADDON_KEY_TO_SKU has no pin proving every legacy key is bridged -- a future unbridged key keying its advisory lock on the raw string re-opens the admin/tenant lock divergence.

title: Charge loop + dunning must introduce a non-payment signal (B327 successor, Phase 1 design)
symptom: suspendOverdueTenants() filters stripeSubId: { not: null }; the self-serve model never sets it, so every self-serve tenant is structurally invisible to the suspension cron. TenantSubscription.failedPaymentCount and .nextChargeAt are DEAD columns -- zero reads/writes for the former, never persisted for the latter. Owner ruling: the first five customers are free pilots, so 'non-payers are never auto-suspended' is current POLICY (see B327), not a defect. Never close this by dropping the filter -- that would suspend tenants who were never charged. The charge loop must CREATE a non-payment signal, not start reading one. Its grace constant is a local PAYMENT_GRACE_DAYS = 3, not the GRACE_DAYS = 7 in plan-catalog.constants.ts, which belongs to an unrelated soft-cap meter.

title: stop.gate5.spec's F4 leak check asserts count-unchanged instead of creates-no-new-dir
symptom: F4 snapshots the stop-gate5-spec-* tmpdir count before and after, and fails if the count changed. A stale dir left behind by any earlier interrupted run (this host, another session, or a prior failed push) makes the NEXT unrelated push's verify fail on this check even though nothing it did leaked anything. Should instead snapshot the SET of dirs before/after and assert no NEW entry was added, not that the count is unchanged. Found live: a concurrent host verify run transiently pushed the count from 0 to 10 during a rf-F39 push attempt (confirmed not a real leak; count was back to 0 moments later).

title: Webhook downgrade-schedule read for the audit meta happens outside the CAS transaction
symptom: The webhook reinstatement path reads the downgrade schedule for the downgradeLeftArmed audit meta OUTSIDE the CAS transaction; the admin twin reads it inside the transaction. Record-only rigor gap (the audit meta could theoretically race with a concurrent schedule change), no money effect. From the #740 (B216 webhook fix) review.

title: Legacy cohort (planKey null) gets only a log line for a left-armed downgrade schedule, no durable record
location: apps/api/src/billing/billing.service.ts -- emitPayingDelta short-circuit for planKey === null
symptom: For the legacy cohort where planKey === null, emitPayingDelta short-circuits, so the left-armed downgrade schedule is only logger.log'd, not durably recorded (unlike the normal cohort's audit meta). From the #740 (B216 webhook fix) review.

title: A downgrade due during a lapse applies up to ~24h late after reactivation, with no UI surface
location: billing cron (02:00 pass) vs tenant reactivation
symptom: A downgrade that comes due WHILE a tenant is lapsed applies on the next 02:00 cron pass after reactivation -- up to ~24h still on the old plan/entitlements -- with nothing telling the tenant. Intended behavior per the owner's ruling (not a defect), but flagged as a W5 candidate: the delay wants a UI surface. From the #740 (B216 webhook fix) review.

title: bugs.mjs self-test asserts a wall-clock bound on a race, not just its ordering
symptom: The lock-order self-test asserts the race finished in under 5s; under host load the ordering/exit assertions pass but the timer bound fails, giving false reds on busy hosts (sibling of B411 -- asserting on ambient machine state instead of the behaviour under test; hit 4+ times tonight during concurrent host verify runs). Fix: drop the wall-clock bound -- the ordering assertion is the actual proof.

title: Convert to Invoice navigated to /invoices/undefined — the page read invoiceId from a response keyed id (alias B15-NAV, linked to B15)
symptom: After a successful estimate→invoice convert the detail page pushed router.push('/invoices/undefined') because useConvertEstimate typed the result { invoiceId } while POST /estimates/:id/convert-to-invoice returns the created Invoice keyed id. Fixed in aa47ee9e (F27): result typed { id }, navigation only when an id is present. Sibling of B15 (convert offered when it cannot succeed).

title: SKIP_VERIFY docs-only auto-detector diffs against stale @{u} after a rebase, forcing a hand-written reason on a genuinely docs-only push
symptom: Hit live on #746: after rebasing fix/F39-payments onto master, @{u} (origin/fix/F39-payments) was still pinned to the pre-rebase tip because that exact push had not yet landed. git diff --name-only "$upstream"...HEAD therefore included every commit the rebase replayed in, so SKIP_VERIFY=1 with no reason was refused even though the branch's actual new content (diff vs origin/master) was 100% docs. Fix: diff against git merge-base origin/master HEAD instead of/in addition to @{u} when they disagree -- the merge-base is unaffected by whether this branch's own remote-tracking ref has caught up yet.

title: prod-migrate-script.spec.ts asserts a subprocess exit status that becomes null under host-load timeout, not a wrong-value failure
symptom: expect(res.status).toBe(2) fails with 'Received: null' under severe concurrent host load. Node's spawnSync kills the child and returns status:null when its timeout option fires -- a real, correct exit code silently becomes indistinguishable from a hang. A generous 30s bound was still exceeded under this session's own multi-worktree concurrent-verify load. Sibling of B225/B244 (ci-freshness-guard-script.spec.ts's own host-load timing flakes, tracked separately) -- same underlying class (a test's bounded wait is still an ambient-machine-load assumption), different mechanism (subprocess timeout vs an in-test wall-clock assertion). Fix direction: raise the timeout with documented rationale, assert res.signal===null as a precondition surfacing a distinguishable 'harness timeout' message, or a bounded retry.

title: Repo-wide npm run format / broad lint-staged globs churn files a commit never touched, including the machine-managed bug registry
location: root package.json 'format' script (repo-wide prettier), .lintstagedrc.json glob *.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mjs,cjs,json,md,yaml,yml,css} (runs on every staged file in a commit, not just the ones the change intends)
symptom: Hit repeatedly this session: bugs.mjs's own tags-array serialization (no space after comma) gets flipped to spaced by lint-staged's prettier --write on ANY commit touching the same directory, even when that file was untouched by the actual change -- observed on B388.md/B389.md across multiple unrelated commits. Separately, master itself carries at least two files (validate-code-map.stamp.self-test.mjs, code-map/api/root-tooling-campaign-infrastructure.md, both from #747/B420) that are not prettier-clean per a fresh checkout's lint-staged pass -- confirmed not a config drift (that PR was pushed with the verify skip), but it means ANY later commit that happens to touch those paths will show spurious reformatting churn. Fix: add .claude/campaign/** and .claude/lessons/** to .prettierignore (registry data owns its own exact serialization, same precedent as the already-prettier-ignored vendored skill scripts); separately, engine/builder commits should format only the paths they actually intend to change, not rely on a repo-wide format pass.

title: validate-code-map.stamp.self-test.mjs spawned git with inherited GIT_* env — under the pre-push hook it renamed a live worktree's branch and rewrote .git/config
symptom: Under the pre-push hook, git had already exported GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE (+8 siblings) into the process environment; the self-test's git()/runScript() helpers spawned git for a THROWAWAY scratch repo without scrubbing them, so git honored the inherited GIT_DIR over the scratch cwd -- the fixture's git operations landed on the REAL repo instead. Live incident (22:35Z 2026-09-14): .git/config flipped to core.bare=true/repositoryformatversion=0/[user] self-test@example.invalid, and a live worktree's branch (fix/mobile-scan-lanes) was renamed twice (-> feature/drift -> feature/map-touched) with 3 fixture commits stacked on top of the real head. Already fixed: PR #747 (a3d73ab9) scrubs all 10 GIT_* vars in both helpers, adds a post-init 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel resolves inside scratch' guard, and a REG-B420 victim-repo test proving a second polluting repo's branches/HEAD/config stay byte-unchanged. Lesson L-139 already recorded.

title: Credit note applied to an invoice is shown as 'Paid' everywhere, and counted as cash received in the bookkeeping cash-flow report
location: apps/api/src/invoices/payment-predicates.ts:40 sumConfirmed() (choke point, no method filter); apps/api/src/bookkeeping/bookkeeping.service.ts:1018-1043 getCashFlow() totalIn
symptom: Client-reported (tenant identity removed): an invoice with a return credit note applied shows 'Paid to date -$638.00' and 'Paid $638.00' although the customer never paid anything -- the $638 is a credit note applied to the invoice. Root cause (verified against master fbec7b7b): credit-notes.service.ts creates a real InvoicePayment row (method: CREDIT_NOTE, status: PAID); payment-predicates.ts:40 sumConfirmed() sums every status===PAID row with NO method filter, and invoices.service.ts (list :3073, detail :3304) derive paidAmount/balanceDue from it. Only per-row labels (Payment History card, PDF row, bookkeeping void/CN reconciliation) read method -- no TOTAL does. Conflates across web invoice detail/list, invoice PDF, buyer portal (also double-counts DRAFT via a separate status!==VOID reduce), mobile customer/operator invoice, customers detail, buyer statement, and bookkeeping summary. MONEY REPORT DEFECT: bookkeeping cash-flow's totalIn (verified :1018-1043, payments fetched with status:PAID and no method filter, summed directly) counts a credit-note application as cash received. Fix design (Fable, brief local-assets/handoff/2026-09-14/LAUNCH-credit-applied-vs-paid.md): add splitConfirmed() returning {cash, creditApplied, advanceApplied} next to sumConfirmed; paidAmount becomes cash-only, new creditApplied/advanceApplied fields on the invoice DTO in packages/types/api; wording splits into 'Payments received' + 'Credits applied' (operator) / 'Credit issued -- CN-...' (customer-facing); cash-flow totalIn becomes cash-methods-only; buyer portal's DRAFT-counting reduce replaced with the confirmed-only predicate. Full surface list, rulings and red-first REG-B421 test plan in the brief.

title: npm run local:e2e reports exit 0 while Playwright actually failed — the local-env.mjs e2e wrapper masks the child's exit code
location: scripts/local-env.mjs --e2e (spawnSync wrapper around npm --prefix apps/web run test:e2e)
symptom: Seen on the F27 stack gate: npm run local:e2e exited 0 while Playwright itself reported 7 failed / 4 skipped / 14 passed for the run. local-env.mjs's own spawnSync call does 'process.exit(res.status ?? 1)', which should propagate the child's real exit status -- the exact masking point within the npm --prefix / nested npm run / playwright chain needs confirming by whoever fixes this, since the wrapper's own exit-forwarding line reads correct in isolation. Third wrapper-exit-code incident in this session's lane (same class as L-103 'a piped/wrapped gate command can discard its real exit code' and the SKIP_VERIFY wrapper trap). Fix: propagate the child's real exit status end-to-end through the whole chain; add a self-test that a deliberately-failing project still turns the wrapper's own exit code non-zero.

title: Local e2e lane targets tenant e2e-routeflow but local:seed only seeds tenant test — all 7 F27-gate failures are 'no data', not real regressions
symptom: Verified: local-env.mjs's --e2e mode hardcodes PLAYWRIGHT_TENANT_SLUG=e2e-routeflow, but apps/api/prisma/seed.ts (the local:seed target) only creates/seeds tenant slug 'test'. Every local e2e run against a freshly-seeded compose stack therefore has no data for e2e-routeflow, producing 7 F27-gate failures that all trace to missing data, not real regressions: CP-01 (its amount regex reads the empty-state text as an amount), CP-09/REG-B154 (empty products), ESC-01/ESC-02/BOXED-01 (no customer found), and REG-B130 (a strict-mode .or() locator, ambiguous when the page is in its empty state). Master's prod E2E (a real run against seeded prod-equivalent data) passed the identical specs -- confirms this is a local-lane data mismatch, not a product regression. Fix: seed e2e-routeflow locally (or point the local e2e lane at test instead), and separately harden CP-01's amount regex to not match empty-state text and fix REG-B130's ambiguous .or() locator so an empty-state page fails clearly instead of ambiguously.

title: edit-items staged-edit snapshot uses a raw AsyncStorage keyspace instead of the shared user-scoped persist store (documented R1 deviation)
symptom: By design (per the code's own comments and RULINGS.md R1, mobile scan-to-order hunt): the staged-edit snapshot is a KEYSPACE (one key per order, rf.edit-items.v1:<userId|anon>:<orderId>) written directly to AsyncStorage, not through lib/user-scoped-storage.ts's clearUserScopedStorage helper used by the zustand-persisted stores -- because that module imports AsyncStorage at the top level, which edit-items-draft.ts 'may not' (unstated bundling/import-cycle constraint, never verified). Sign-out cleanup is therefore a bespoke getAllKeys() prefix-sweep in session-teardown.ts instead of the standard one-call helper -- a second cleanup mechanism to keep in sync with the standard one, and a second place the B136/B137/B140 class of cross-user leak could reappear if either drifts. Follow-up: migrate to a user-scoped persist store (resolve or route around the stated import-cycle constraint) so this snapshot uses the same one cleanup mechanism as every other persisted store.

title: edit-items cold open reads the anon-scoped staged-edit snapshot before auth resolves, then re-reads the real user's snapshot a moment later
symptom: snapshotKey = editItemsSnapshotKey(id, userId) is computed at render time; on cold open/deep link userId is undefined until auth resolves (the screen's own comment at :522 says so), so the restore effect at :429 (AsyncStorage.getItem(snapshotKey), deps=[snapshotKey]) fires FIRST against the anon-prefixed key, then fires AGAIN once userId resolves and snapshotKey changes to the real user-scoped key. The WRITE path is guarded (:525 returns early while userId==null), but the READ is not -- if a stale or another-session's anon-scoped snapshot exists, it can populate the screen briefly before the correct user-scoped read overwrites it moments later. Follow-up: guard the read effect the same way the write effect already is (skip AsyncStorage.getItem until userId has resolved, or never write/leave a readable anon-scoped snapshot in the first place once the store migrates per B424).

title: bugs.mjs has no lawful transition for a mis-tiered proven row (proven -> already-fixed; reopen forces regressed)
location: scripts/campaign/bugs.mjs cmds["already-fixed"] (state guard: queued/in-flight only), cmds.reopen (only exit from proven, forces state:regressed + a mandatory regression citation)
symptom: Hit live on B420: a T1 row was correctly proven, but its proof cited evidence in a shape campaign-check.mjs cannot verify (a standalone node self-test run by npm run verify, never a jest suite -- tier T1's discharge path scans jest report titles only). The correct target state is already-fixed (its EVIDENCE_ONLY_STATES path in campaign-check.mjs checks only that evidence is non-empty, matching this evidence's real shape), but no command reaches it from proven: already-fixed refuses any state other than queued/in-flight, and the only command that clears a proven row's proof (reopen) forces state to regressed and REQUIRES citing an actual failing REG-token or regression run -- writing that citation for a bug that did NOT regress (it is correctly fixed, just mistiered) would be a fabricated claim. Fixed this one instance via a direct, lock-checked, single-field edit to its ledger row (owner-approved, out of band) -- a manual escape hatch that should not need repeating. Fix: add a lawful transition (e.g. a 'reclassify <B###> already-fixed --pr <n> --why <text>' command, or extend already-fixed to accept a proven row when explicitly told the tier/evidence-shape was wrong, distinct from reopen's regression semantics) so this never again requires a direct ledger edit.

title: Staged dev-pipeline engine does not enforce agent workdir -- implementers wrote six files into the main checkout instead of their isolated worktree
location: dev-pipeline skill engine (outside this repo) -- fixed in skills commits 49c4ceb and a961014
symptom: The staged engine's per-task workdir was advisory text only, not enforced. Lite lane implementers (2026-09-14, Lite L1 flavor-print session) wrote six files directly into the MAIN checkout instead of their assigned isolated tree. Evidence patch: local-assets/handoff/2026-09-14/lite-plan/stray-main-checkout-buyer-notes-0551Z.patch. Already fixed via skills commits 49c4ceb and a961014 (outside this repo, no PR number here to cite) -- engine re-staged with the fix (sha256 857a9d4d..., 199,257 B).

title: The pre-push verify chain's self-tests modify real .claude/campaign/bugs/*.md in the working tree while they run
location: npm run verify chain -- self-test scripts touching the real registry (B420/B426/B388/B389 observed) -- same class as B420's GIT_DIR leak
symptom: Observed repeatedly this session (self-referential commit backfill lines appearing on B388.md/B389.md/B420.md/B426.md after running node scripts/campaign/bugs.mjs self-test / the verify chain, before any commit) and again on routeflow-33's push of #743 at ~06:25Z. Same class as B420: a fixture/self-test process writing into the REAL repo state instead of a properly isolated scratch copy. Unlike B420's GIT_DIR leak (a full repo hijack), this specific instance is bugs.mjs's own sync-on-verify step touching real .md files as a side effect of its own commit-scan -- appears to be sync's intended behavior (Gate 4 of stop.mjs runs sync every turn) rather than a leak, but the pre-push verify chain running it mid-verify, before commit, means a push can pick up working-tree changes nobody explicitly authored in that turn. Needs investigation: is this sync's documented idempotent behavior working as intended, or a self-test fixture writing outside its scratch dir the way B420's stamp self-test did.

title: IdempotencyKey rows have no cleanup
location: mobile scan-to-order PR-2 (lane D) -- IdempotencyKey table
symptom: F7, relayed from mobile PR-2's review (routeflow-f8 / Routeflow sessions credit recovery lane): IdempotencyKey rows are written to dedupe retried mutations but nothing ever deletes or expires them -- unbounded table growth. Not independently root-caused by the registry minter; owned by the PR-2 lane for the actual fix design (TTL, a scheduled sweep job, or expiry on read).

title: mrr.service ledgerMrr/momDelta count soft-deleted tenants' historical billing events -- deleteTenant books no offsetting delta
location: apps/api/src/billing/mrr.service.ts:70-71 (ledgerAgg/momAgg billingEvent.aggregate, no deletedAt filter); apps/api/src/platform-admin/platform-admin.service.ts:340-359 deleteTenant
symptom: Verified against master d69f3094: mrr.service.ts's ledgerAgg = this.prisma.billingEvent.aggregate({ _sum: { amountDelta: true } }) and momAgg (same aggregate, createdAt >= monthAgo) have NO where-clause filtering by tenant status or deletedAt -- unlike every other query in the same Promise.all (subs/addons/trialTenants/readOnlyTenants all filter deletedAt: null). deleteTenant (platform-admin.service.ts:340) sets deletedAt + status:CANCELLED but never writes a BillingEvent/amountDelta row to offset the tenant's prior positive contribution. Net effect: ledgerMrr and momDelta permanently overstate MRR by the sum of every deleted tenant's historical billing events, forever, with no correction mechanism. #743 review finding F5. Fix: scope both aggregates to non-deleted tenants (a join/filter on tenant.deletedAt), or book an offsetting negative delta in deleteTenant.

title: reconcilePriceLedger and updateTenantPriceOverride's backfill can both book a +price delta for the same price change during a reconciliation backfill
symptom: Verified against master d69f3094: reconcilePriceLedger (billing.service.ts:447) reads tenantSubscription.basePriceSnapshot, computes oldMonthly vs newMonthly, then writes the new snapshot and emits a PLAN_CHANGED amountDelta -- as three SEPARATE, unserialized operations with no  and no lock. updateTenantPriceOverride's backfillBase branch (platform-admin.service.ts:1099-1123) independently reads the SAME basePriceSnapshot field, and when it observes null, books its OWN +price delta (amountDelta: roundMoney(dto.monthly!)) inside its own . Neither path takes a row lock or advisory lock against the other. If an admin re-prices a tenant (updateTenantPriceOverride) while reconcilePriceLedger's backfill is mid-flight for the same tenant, both can observe the pre-backfill null/stale basePriceSnapshot and both book a +price amountDelta for what is really one price change -- double-booking MRR growth. #743 review finding (reviews/743-fix-fable-seam.md, seam B). Fix: serialize both paths through the same lock/CAS discipline the rest of billing.service.ts uses (the tenant-keyed advisory lock, or a conditional updateMany on the prior basePriceSnapshot value).

title: BillingEventService.emit defaults amountDelta to null instead of requiring an explicit choice at every call site
symptom: Verified against master d69f3094: emit()'s opts type declares amountDelta?: number | null (optional) and the write is amountDelta: opts?.amountDelta ?? null -- a call site that forgets to pass amountDelta silently books a billing event with zero money impact instead of failing to compile or throwing. Every MRR/reconciliation figure (mrr.service.ts's ledgerMrr/momDelta) sums this field directly, so a silently-null delta at any call site is invisible in every downstream money report with no signal it happened. Fix: make amountDelta required at the type level (drop the ? and the ?? null fallback) so a new call site is forced to explicitly pass 0 or a real value, never silently default.

title: momDelta reports a reconciliation backfill's one-time correction events as 30-day MRR growth
symptom: Verified against master d69f3094: momAgg = this.prisma.billingEvent.aggregate({ _sum: { amountDelta: true }, where: { createdAt: { gte: monthAgo } } }) sums EVERY billingEvent in the trailing 30 days with no filter distinguishing organic MRR movement (new subs, real price changes, churn) from one-time reconciliation/backfill corrections (e.g. reconcilePriceLedger's PLAN_CHANGED emission, or updateTenantPriceOverride's backfillBase emission -- see the sibling rows filed alongside this one). If a reconciliation backfill runs and emits amountDelta events correcting historically-null basePriceSnapshot values, momDelta reports that one-time correction as real month-over-month growth, inflating the momentum figure shown to whoever reads MRR reporting. Fix: tag reconciliation/backfill-sourced billing events distinctly (a payload field or event subtype) and exclude them from momDelta's window, or report them as a separate 'reconciliation' line rather than folding them into organic growth.

title: Compose container names are hard-coded, so every worktree's local stack fights over the same fixed names (project-name collision)
location: docker-compose.yml (6 container_name entries, routeflow_* prefix, no top-level name:)
symptom: Verified against master 97fdb372: docker-compose.yml has 6 hard-coded container_name entries (routeflow_postgres, routeflow_redis, routeflow_redis_ui, routeflow_migrate, routeflow_api, routeflow_web) and no top-level name: field. Without an explicit -p <project> flag, the compose project name defaults to the invoking directory's basename -- but the fixed container_name values collide across ANY two worktrees/checkouts that both run local:up, regardless of project name. Already documented as L-103's root cause (2026-09-10); recurs at every lane handoff since nothing has actually changed the compose file. Fix: add a top-level name: routeflow (or require -p routeflow on every local:* script) so at most one stack can hold the fixed container names at a time, with a clear collision error instead of a silent fight.

title: shareCsv() ignores downloadAsync's HTTP status, the same gap #756 fixed for print and share PDF
symptom: Verified against master 97fdb372: shareCsv() (line 464) destructures only { uri } from FileSystem.downloadAsync(url, target), discarding status entirely. The sibling call site at line 244-245 (sharePdf, fixed by #756) destructures { uri, status } and checks isDownloadOk(status) immediately after, failing loudly on a non-2xx download. shareCsv silently proceeds to share/write a failed download's response body (an error page, an empty file) as if it were the real CSV. Fix: apply the same isDownloadOk(status) check to shareCsv's downloadAsync call that sharePdf already has.

title: List pages sharing one useMutation() hook's .mutate() across per-row callbacks lose all but the last row's callback (L-148 class) -- unaudited sibling sweep

symptom: L-148 (2026-09-15) fixed invoices/page.tsx's row Print (TanStack Query v5's useMutation() is a single observer per hook instance -- concurrent .mutate(id, {onSuccess,...}) calls share that state, so an earlier row's callbacks are silently overwritten by whichever row's mutate() fires last, not accumulated) but flagged its own fix as unaudited beyond that one call site. Ran L-148's own suggested sweep against master 97fdb372: grep -rn '\.mutate\([a-zA-Z].*{$' apps/web/app --include=*.tsx returns 80 raw hits. Per L-148's guard note, most are single-instance and safe -- this row is the audit itself: narrow to .map()-rendered LIST rows sharing one hook instance before treating any hit as a real instance of the bug, then fix each confirmed instance the same way (mutateAsync + local try/catch/finally).

title: The repo guard hook's worktree-cwd exemption trusts the hook payload's cwd field, which can report the session-start checkout root instead of the current shell cwd after a cd into a worktree
symptom: Verified guard.mjs's own logic against the current file: effectiveCwd = typeof cwd === string && cwd ? cwd : process.cwd() trusts whatever cwd the PreToolUse hook payload reports, with no independent verification against the actual current shell directory; looksLikeWorktreeCwd() then just regex-tests that string for /worktree/i to decide whether git checkout -b is exempted from the shared-checkout-stranding block. Reported live (a helper session hit the block and bypassed it with GUARD_ALLOW=1) as: after cd-ing from the main checkout into a worktree, the hook's reported cwd still read as the main checkout root, not the worktree path, so the exemption never triggered and a legitimate worktree-local git checkout -b was blocked. Not independently reproduced by the registry minter this session -- every git checkout -B call here ran with an already-worktree-rooted cwd and was never blocked, so this is a report to verify, not a confirmed repro. Fix direction: have the hook independently resolve the real cwd (e.g. via the tool_input's own cwd field if the harness provides one separately from the session-level cwd, or via git rev-parse --show-toplevel/--git-common-dir from the command's actual execution directory) rather than trusting a single payload field that may lag a mid-session cd.

title: campaign-check reports a MISSING workspace jest report as the generic no test titled with REG- error instead of naming the missing report
symptom: Verified against master 27073859: campaign-check only fails loudly with a clear message when ALL FOUR workspace reports (api/mobile/pricing/web) are simultaneously null (:739-750). When only ONE or a FEW are missing, jestIndex is built via mergeIndexes(indexAssertions(jestAssertions(api),...), ...) -- a null workspace contributes zero entries to the merged index, indistinguishable from a report that EXISTS but genuinely has no REG-{id} hit. Any row whose REG token lives specifically in the missing workspace's report then fails at checkProofHits (:939) with the generic 'no test titled with REG-{id} found in the {sourceLabel} report', which reads as 'this test doesn't exist' rather than 'this workspace's report was never generated'. Hit 3 times tonight in fresh worktrees per the report. Fix: when jestIndex is built, track which of the 4 workspaces contributed a null report and, in checkProofHits, if hits.length===0 AND the row's expected workspace's report was null, fail with 'report missing for <workspace>' instead of the generic message.

title: Buyer layout locks pinch-zoom (maximumScale:1, userScalable:false) — WCAG 1.4.4
symptom: apps/web/app/buyer/layout.tsx's viewport export sets maximumScale:1 and userScalable:false, disabling pinch-to-zoom for every buyer-portal page. This fails WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.4 (Resize Text) — a low-vision user on the buyer portal cannot zoom in at all, unlike every other shell (the root layout deliberately avoids this restriction).

title: ScanOrderSheet's stale not-found pill is never cleared by a later successful scan
symptom: A 'No product for X' error pill could remain visible up to 8s after a later scan succeeded -- the success path never called dismissError, so the operator sees a false not-found at the exact moment the item was actually added.

title: Camera scan and the same code typed in search can add a line twice
symptom: The camera-scan settled effect and the search-box scan handler shared no accept guard, and the camera path never cleared the search field it was resolving from -- a wedge/Enter scan racing the camera path could add the same product twice.

title: A no-terminator wedge scan silently does nothing
symptom: productSearchParams always sent a plain-text search term even for a scanned barcode, and the server treats search/scanCode as mutually exclusive lookups -- a wedge scan with no Enter terminator (or a decode-length mismatch, e.g. iOS 13-digit vs a 12-digit stored UPC-A) produced no line, no error, and no beep.

title: Leaving the order-edit item screen discards all staged edits with no warning
symptom: Both the header back button and Android hardware back called router.back() directly with no confirmation and no autosave, silently discarding every staged qty/price/substitution edit on the screen.

title: FormSheet's dirty-discard guard is wired to a no-op on native
symptom: warnIfDirty was wired only to a web-only beforeunload listener that native never fires, and handleCancel never read it at all -- two callers (payments/record, standing-orders/new) additionally passed a bare true instead of a real dirty check, so the confirm affordance was a no-op everywhere on the phone.

title: A reason-only edit to an overridden order line is silently dropped
symptom: buildOrderItemDiff only emitted overrideReason when the price itself had also changed, so editing just the reason on an already-overridden line showed as saved in the UI but sent nothing to the server; the server's individual-UPDATE branch had the mirror bug, writing overrideReason only inside its isManualOverride spread.

title: The new-order scan tray has no price control at all
symptom: A line added via the scan tray on NewOrderScreen/invoices-new had no way to edit its price without first leaving scan mode and opening the full cart modal.

title: A $0 unlisted cart line stays visible but is silently dropped from the order
symptom: The POST payload builder filtered unlisted lines on unitPrice > 0, so a deliberately free/promotional $0 line rendered and counted in the on-screen cart but never reached the server -- web and the DTO both allow $0.

title: Local barcode scan matching can resolve to the wrong or an archived product
symptom: The local fast-path scan match used a bare .find() with no isActive check and no disambiguation, so a code shared between an active and an archived product (allowed by the per-column unique constraints) silently resolved by page order, and a genuine cross-field collision (one product's sku equal to another's barcode) was never surfaced to the operator.

title: Applying a credit note to an order doesn't refresh the credit-notes list
symptom: useCreateOrderAsDriver and useUpdateOrderItems never invalidated the ['credit-notes'] query key, so when the server silently clamped an over-applied credit amount, the mobile UI kept showing the original requested amount with no indication it had been reduced.

title: Editing order items resyncs the linked invoice server-side with no client notification
symptom: resyncOrderInvoicesForEdit rebuilt a linked invoice's items/total after an order-item edit but emitted no invoice.updated socket event and the edit mutation invalidated no invoice query key, so a mounted invoice screen kept showing the stale total.

title: The phone never learns when a product's price or active state changes
symptom: No product.* socket event existed and TanStack's focusManager was never wired to AppState, so a backgrounded/foregrounded phone could keep quoting a stale price or a deactivated product for its 5-minute staleTime with no way to learn otherwise (display-only -- the server re-prices non-overridden lines for real).

title: Product picker fetches a full catalog page before the operator types or scans anything
symptom: NewOrderScreen and invoices/new fetched page 1 (50 rows) at screen mount and rendered it quiet; edit-items and recurring-invoices/new fetched the same 50 rows on picker open and rendered them immediately -- the intended no-fetch-until-the-operator-acts behavior existed nowhere.

title: ProductPickerSheet fetches the entire catalog with no gate
symptom: useAdminProducts was called from the component body with limit: 0 (fetch-all) and no enabled flag, so the whole catalog loaded at parent-screen mount for standing-orders/new and at picker-open for edit-items' nested sheet even though React Native's Modal keeps invisible children mounted.

title: invoices/[id]/edit's discard confirm is wired to a hardcoded true
symptom: confirmDiscardIfDirty was passed a bare true instead of a real dirty check, so the discard-confirm prompt fired even with no unsaved changes and gave no distinguishing signal when there genuinely were some.

title: Purchase-order receive discards typed deltas/notes with no warning
symptom: The receive screen had no touched-state tracking, so leaving after typing quantity deltas or notes (fields that are otherwise pre-seeded) lost them silently with no discard confirmation.

title: SearchBar has no autofocus, so the first scan of a session can land nowhere
symptom: SearchBar took no autoFocus prop and forwarded no ref, so a wedge scanner's first keystrokes right after opening a search view could arrive before the input had focus and land nowhere.

title: Order-creation modal has no barcode scanner; placeholder promises one
symptom: The product-search input's placeholder reads 'Search by name, SKU or scan barcode...' but no scan control is wired in — every other product-search surface (inventory, invoices, vendor-bills, products list/detail, ProductCreateModal, InlineCreateProductModal, StockCountTab) pairs the identical placeholder with BarcodeScannerButton. Owner-reported on mobile web as 'the barcode mark is not there anymore'.

title: AdminModal lacks dialog accessibility semantics -- no role, no focus trap, no focus restore
symptom: The shared modal used across every platform-admin surface (tenant detail, feature console, override drawers) had no role=dialog/aria-modal, no Tab/Shift-Tab focus trap, no initial focus on open, and no focus restoration to the triggering element on close -- a keyboard/screen-reader user could tab out of an open modal into the page behind it, and focus was lost entirely on close.

title: A denied tenant deep-linking to /invoices/recurring gets a raw 403 instead of the graceful plan lock
symptom: PLAN_GATED_NAV had no entry for /invoices/recurring even though the route carries its own server-side @RequirePlanFlag("flag.recurring_invoices") gate -- every other plan-gated route shows a graceful lock via this client-side mirror map, but this one route was missing from it entirely, so a denied tenant hitting it deep-link or via nav got an unhandled 403.

title: Demo booking availability doesn't distinguish unconfigured from fully booked
symptom: When Google Calendar integration is unconfigured or unreachable in prod, getAvailability() returns {days: []} identically to a genuinely fully-booked window. demo-scheduler.tsx renders the same 'No times are available this month... email us' message for both, so visitors and support cannot tell a broken integration from a busy calendar.

title: Deliveries/new has no mobile-optimized layout — desktop map+sidebar unusable below lg
symptom: Owner-requested redesign: below lg, the map is the canvas and a bottom sheet (peek/half/full detents) holds stops/route options/actions; desktop keeps the existing side-by-side layout, split via a JS isMobile boolean (a CSS-only split would mount two billable Google Maps instances).

title: Marketing site: scroll-reveal sections stuck invisible + 4 contrast failures below AA
symptom: Live P1: .editorial-reveal sections (9 capability cards, section headings, wholesale-extras) never reached opacity 1 after scroll on /, /product, /wholesalers — CSS never declared an explicit revealed-opacity rule, only the reveal-pending=0 rule, relying on an implicit cascade fallback that failed in production. Separately, 4 text roles measured below WCAG AA: the operation-story widget heading (dark navy on dark navy, 1.09-1.61:1), the purple AI-scan card heading+paragraph (1.33-1.61:1), the --g-soft caption token (3.58:1), and the difference-section intro paragraphs (1.63:1) -- all traced to same-specificity CSS rules whose winner depended on stylesheet import/chunk order rather than being deterministic.

title: Middleware proxied platform-admin and verify-email to the mobile-web app with no Expo counterpart
symptom: middleware.ts proxies phone user-agents to the Expo mobile-web app for everything outside an allowlist. /admin-login, every /admin/* path, and /verify-email were not on it and have no Expo screen at all, so a real phone hitting them got an Unmatched Route from the wrong app -- this is why the owner could not use the backoffice on their phone.

title: Orders list delivery date-range filter overflows the viewport at 390px
symptom: The delivery date-range filter's own container never wrapped, unlike every other filter control on the same row, so its to field ran past the viewport edge at 390px and was unreachable on a phone.

title: Marketing contrast sweep round 2 — 8 selectors still fail WCAG AA after B504
symptom: B504 fixed 4 of 28 original contrast violations but only covered headings, not their sibling elements sharing the same specificity-tie mechanism. Round-2 audit (local-assets/proofs/2026-09-17/mobile-audit/round2/contrast-round2.json) found 12 findings (8 unique selector/color pairs) still failing AA: .ai-assisted-step small (tie, never extended from its h3/p siblings), .story-explanation > p on the operation-story dark scrubber (same tie mechanism, different widget), .record-note span/p (--g-eyebrow/--g-soft tokens one shade too light for #eee2fa), .audience-card .text-link and .passport-bottom > span:last-child (plain undertones), and .retailer-art figcaption (a correct white-on-scrim photo caption clobbered by an unrelated shared !important rule).

title: driver_payments can be granted with neither recurring_routes nor order_delivery active, leaving an addon on with no route surface to use it
location: apps/api/src/billing/feature-registry.ts (driver_payments row, requires: {anyOf:[recurring_routes,order_delivery]}); apps/web/app/(platform-admin)/admin/tenants/[id]/page.tsx (legacy AVAILABLE_ADDONS toggle) and _features/EnableAddonModal.tsx (B2b Enable-as-add-on action)
symptom: The feature registry declares driver_payments requires anyOf [recurring_routes, order_delivery], but nothing enforces that dependency client-side: the legacy toggle card and the new Feature Console 'Enable as add-on' modal both POST /platform-admin/tenants/:id/addons/enable for driver_payments unconditionally, with no check for whether the tenant already holds one of its two prerequisite addons. A super-admin can enable driver_payments alone, leaving the tenant billed/flagged for at-door payment collection with no route surface (Dispatch or Deliveries) where a driver would ever reach the gated endpoint (POST /route-runs/:id/stops/:stopId/complete-with-payment). Pre-existing behavior, carried forward unchanged by B2b (PR #872) rather than introduced by it -- found during that ticket's B2b/ticket-4 analysis, filed per lead allocation.

title: Marketing scroll-reveal (.editorial-reveal/.reveal-pending) may be inert — opacity:0 rule never observed to apply
symptom: Local dev testing (fresh npm run dev, .next cache cleared, prefers-reduced-motion confirmed 'no-preference' via matchMedia) shows .capability-card and .section-heading elements get the '.editorial-reveal reveal-pending' classes added by editorial-motion.tsx's IntersectionObserver setup as expected, but getComputedStyle always reports opacity:1 regardless of whether '.reveal-pending' is present — toggling the class on/off in the live DOM makes no observable difference. Reproduced on BOTH new content (WholesalerCapabilities cards added in PR #871) AND untouched pre-existing content (WorkflowTour's 'SEE YOUR WORKFLOW IN ROUTEFLOW' section-heading, unedited by that PR) — so this is not specific to the new content and predates it. Not yet determined whether the '.editorial-reveal.reveal-pending { opacity: 0 }' rule (marketing.css ~9219) is simply not being reached in the cascade, or something else neutralizes it; not investigated further per instruction. Two possible readings worth distinguishing: (a) a genuine dev-mode-only artifact with no production impact, or (b) the mechanism is already inert in production too, which would mean an earlier fix for a *different* bug (content stuck invisible at opacity:0) was resolved by disabling the reveal system rather than correcting it, and the safe failure direction (always visible) has been masking that ever since. Needs live verification against a real (non-dev, ideally deployed) build before concluding either way.

title: Order edit-mode line-item name column starves to unreadable width at 390px
symptom: Flex row with no wrap: Qty (label+input), the price column (w-20 shrink-0), and action buttons all hold their content width, so the one flexible column (product name, flex-1 min-w-0) absorbs all shrink pressure. With a long custom item name the name input collapses to 16-18px wide (scrollWidth 738px vs clientWidth 16px) -- visually empty and unreadable. Content starvation, a different mechanism from B513's page-level overflow.

title: Demo-booking internal notification recipient should be a configurable list, not one address
symptom: B518 shipped a single-address code-side default (hello@routeflow.info) for the internal demo-booking notification. Owner feedback: point it at admin@routeflow.info instead, and add a second (colleague) recipient -- which a single-string config value cannot express.

title: Buyer portal order detail — items table is clipped horizontally with no horizontal scroll at mobile width
location: buyer/customer portal order detail page, Items table (PRODUCT/ORDERED/DELIVERED/REMAINING columns)
symptom: Owner report on a real phone-width viewport (2026-09-18), buyer/customer portal, order ORD-00004: opening an order shows the Items table cut off at the right edge -- the REMAINING column's values are sliced mid-digit and anything to the right is unreachable. Table does not scroll horizontally. Product names wrap 5-6 lines each, so 3 line items fill the whole screen. Owner's words: 'I cannot see all the details of that order. Horizontally it is not sliding. It seems like it can improve a lot.' Evidence screenshot: C:\Users\nakram\.claude\uploads\20f39e54-c9b5-4469-a28a-cb7ec44dff13\ff0f5119-image.jpg. title: Detail-screen info/pricing-tier grids force grid-cols-2/3/4/5 at 390px with no responsive qualifier
symptom: 390px mobile audit (local-assets/proofs/2026-09-17/mobile-audit/REPORT.md): unqualified grid-cols-2/3/4/5 in five of the six detail screens' (order excluded) info and pricing-tier grids force multi-column layouts into a phone width. Renumbered again B523 -> B534: B523 was independently claimed by #896 17 minutes earlier; id correction only, no behavior change.)

title: Icon-only dashboard buttons have no 44x44 CSS px minimum tap target
symptom: 390px mobile audit (local-assets/proofs/2026-09-17/mobile-audit/REPORT.md): icon-only interactive controls across the dashboard detail screens have no minimum hit area, several well under the 44x44 CSS px baseline for reliable touch input. Fixed via a shared TAP_TARGET utility (packages/ui/src/web/utils.ts) composed at each icon-only button call site in orders/[id], invoices/[id], vendor-bills/[id], customers/[id], products/[id] -- returns/[id] has none of this pattern. title: Super-admin Platform Dashboard shows implausible/self-contradicting numbers (MRR vs reconciliation, total users)
location: super-admin platform dashboard (mobile width) -- MRR card + reconciliation subtitle, Total Users card
symptom: Owner report (2026-09-18), super-admin portal at mobile width, screenshot C:\Users\nakram\.claude\uploads\20f39e54-c9b5-4469-a28a-cb7ec44dff13\a3c88d0d-image.jpg: TOTAL TENANTS 26 / ACTIVE 6 (23% of total) / TRIAL 1 / TOTAL USERS 2138 / MRR $0.00, whose own subtitle reads 'Reconciled to ledger: $69.00 - differs by $69.00'. Two distinct smells filed together: (a) the MRR card contradicts itself on screen -- it renders $0.00 while its own reconciliation line says the ledger holds $69.00, so either the MRR query or the reconciliation query is wrong; (b) TOTAL USERS 2138 across only 26 tenants is implausible on its face and its definition needs checking -- it may be counting rows it should not (soft-deleted users, null-tenant rows, every historical user, or cross-tenant duplicates). The known null-tenant-rows issue (~12,357 rows, see project memory) is a candidate cause, not a conclusion. Severity high: the super-admin dashboard is the owner's view of the business: wrong numbers there are decision-grade wrong. Repro only against approved test tenants (test/e2e-routeflow/routeflow-demo/qa-*/e2e-*/ux-audit-*) -- never a live client slug.

title: Tenant tier changes have no before/after preview and don't preserve prior entitlement config across downgrade->upgrade
location: platform-admin tenant tier-change flow (billing/entitlements); intersects apps/api/src/billing/entitlement resolution (preset + grants - denies)
symptom: Owner-requested UX (2026-09-18), feature gap not a defect, filed as two related asks on one entry: (a) changing a tenant's tier gives no before/after preview -- the owner wants to see, before confirming, exactly which features will be ADDED and which will be DROPPED by the change; (b) entitlement configuration must survive a downgrade-then-re-upgrade round trip -- if a tenant had a feature configured a particular way, a downgrade that removes that feature and a later upgrade that restores it should restore it AS IT WAS, not as a fresh default. Flag: (b) intersects the standing ENTITLEMENTS = ONE RULE ruling (preset + grants - denies, owner 2026-09-17, project memory project_entitlements_one_rule_2026-09-17) and may need its own owner ruling on where remembered per-tenant configuration lives -- it is not obviously expressible in preset+grants-denies alone. The lead is raising that intersection with the owner separately; this entry should not be treated as pre-approving a specific storage design.

title: Defect class: multi-column tables wrapped in overflow-hidden clip instead of scrolling at mobile widths
location: repo-wide across buyer-portal and dashboard route families; house pattern (overflow-x-auto wrapper + explicit table min-w) exists at apps/web/app/(dashboard)/vendor-bills/[id]/page.tsx:1256-1257 and is not applied at the instances below

Buyer-portal instances (customer-facing, highest priority): buyer/portal/[seller]/orders/[id]/page.tsx:742 (= B533 itself, filed separately as the worked instance), buyer/portal/[seller]/orders/page.tsx:158, buyer/portal/[seller]/cart/page.tsx:313, buyer/portal/[seller]/shop/page.tsx:569, buyer/portal/[seller]/templates/page.tsx:111. Also matching but not individually enumerated: VariantSplitModal (2 instances), StatementReviewGrid (3), inventory/page (3), CustomerRecordPaymentModal, GroupAsVariantsModal, RecordSupplierPaymentModal, StockCountTab, promotions, finance/reports, settings, shipments, (platform-admin)/admin/buyers/[id]. title: Legacy AVAILABLE_ADDONS toggle UI is dead code (AVAILABLE_ADDONS always empty, superseded by Feature Console) (commit-referenced as B525)
location: apps/web/app/(platform-admin)/admin/tenants/[id]/page.tsx -- AdminModal, toggleAddon, fetchAddons, AddonsTab addon-grid map
