Filed as commit-referenced 'B525' because that id was allocated live by the lead during the window-3 session (paired with B524 = server-side requires enforcement, tracked separately) for exactly this removal, but B525 collides with this tree's own later-filed ids (max B540) and this tool refuses a lower explicit --id -- filed fresh at the next real id instead, per the established B510-style collision protocol, now that the fix (PR #902) has landed.

title: Apex domain routeflow.info (no www) resolves to nothing -- no A/AAAA record published
location: DNS zone for routeflow.info on Google Cloud DNS (registrar/DNS action, not a repo change)
symptom: Verified via DNS-over-HTTPS (2026-09-18): www.routeflow.info resolves fine (CNAME to Railway), but the bare apex routeflow.info returns only an Authority/SOA record from Google Cloud DNS -- no A/AAAA record published at all. The zone exists and is authoritative; nothing is there. Every visitor who types the domain without www gets nothing -- customer-facing. An apex record cannot be a CNAME; this needs an A record (or Railway's documented apex-domain setup, e.g. ALIAS/ANAME if the DNS provider supports it) added to whatever manages the Google Cloud DNS zone. NOT a repo/code change -- a registrar/DNS console action. This has been surfacing as a recurring post-deploy-check warning that nobody owned, which is why it needs an id instead of staying invisible in a log. Specific recommended fix pending from the coordinator -- add when it arrives.

symptom: At the single-column breakpoint (max-width:950px), .booking-copy/.booking-panel are grid items of .booking-layout that default to min-width:auto and refuse to shrink below their own content's min-content width, pinning them ~6px wider than the viewport at 390px — a small horizontal-scroll overflow (scrollWidth 396 vs innerWidth 390), invisible in a screenshot but felt as sideways rubber-banding on scroll. title: Company page feature-grid overflow at tablet width (761-950px)
symptom: On /company between ~761px and ~950px, the .company-principles grid (label column + .feature-grid.three) overflows its .wrap container — visibly broken layout (large empty gutter, misaligned cards), scrollWidth 862 vs innerWidth 768 at the worst point. Root cause is nested implicit min-width:auto grid blowout at TWO levels: .feature-grid is itself a grid item of .company-principles, and .feature-grid's own article children are grid items of .feature-grid — neither shrinks below its content's min-content by default. A scoped min-width:0 fix at both levels (tested locally) cuts the overflow from 94px to 64px but does not eliminate it; a third, smaller overflow then surfaces in one card's own paragraph text. Underlying architecture issue: .company-principles only collapses to a single column at max-width:760px, while its child .feature-grid already collapses from 3 to 2 columns at max-width:900px — the 761-900px band has both mid-collapse and doubly cramped, which is likely the real fix target (align/raise .company-principles's single-column breakpoint) rather than another min-width patch. Found via a production 390/768/1440 viewport sweep across all 11 marketing routes (2026-09-18); NOT fixed this round — needs its own dedicated investigation, filed with full diagnosis for whoever picks it up.

title: activateManualSubscription() can move a tenant into the paying set with no compensating BillingEvent delta (commit-referenced as B545)
location: apps/api/src/platform-admin/platform-admin.service.ts, activateManualSubscription() (~line 773+, Manual subscription activation / non-Stripe payment section)
symptom: Mirror-image of updateStatus()'s gap (the reason mrr can disagree with ledgerMrr on the Platform Dashboard, B536) but in the opposite direction: updateStatus can leave a stale +delta in the ledger after a tenant stops paying; activateManualSubscription can make a tenant START paying (status->ACTIVE + planKey set) without ever emitting the matching +delta, so ledgerMrr can UNDER-count relative to live mrr. Contrast with updatePlan() in the same file, which always emits BILLING_EVENTS.PLAN_CHANGED with a correctly-signed amountDelta in the same transaction as its write. Found during a static review (Opus adversarial pass) for the Platform Dashboard MRR P1 investigation, cross-referenced against billing.service.ts's transitionAndEmit()/emitPayingDelta() pattern -- not yet confirmed as the cause of any specific observed drift, that is a separate question the dashboard investigation (report-mrr-ledger-drift.mjs, PR #912) is still running. Filed as commit-referenced 'B545' because this tree's own later-filed ids (B549/B550, allocated to Lane A concurrently) collide with the originally-given id and this tool refuses a lower explicit --id -- filed fresh at the next real id instead, per the established B510-style collision protocol. Filing only, not fixing.

title: Tenant.plan (legacy display field) and TenantSubscription.planKey (what MRR is actually computed from) can drift -- a tenant onboarded outside the Change Plan UI reports $0 MRR permanently while shown as a paying customer
location: apps/api/src/platform-admin/platform-admin.service.ts (dashboard reads Tenant.plan for display), apps/api/src/billing/mrr.service.ts (priceTenant() gates MRR on TenantSubscription.planKey)
symptom: DB-verified (Lane F, 2026-09-18): Tenant.plan (legacy display field, what the admin UI's plan badge reads) and TenantSubscription.planKey (the field MrrService.priceTenant() actually gates MRR on) can drift. Any tenant onboarded outside the 'Change Plan' UI action has a real Tenant.plan value but no resolved planKey, so it reports $0 MRR forever while the admin UI shows it as a paying customer (e.g. a 'Business' plan badge). Prod has 26 tenants and shows MRR $0.00 -- if most never passed through that control, the platform revenue figure is structurally wrong. Evidence: e2e-routeflow tenant (Tenant.plan=PROFESSIONAL, TenantSubscription.planKey=NULL, contributes $0 permanently); the test tenant before/after a plan-change round-trip (EST. MRR $0 -> $499, planKey resolved PROFESSIONAL->SCALE per the legacy-label-to-catalog-key mapping); two real BillingEvent rows this created (plan.changed $0.00 for Enterprise's custom/no-catalog-price, then plan.changed $499.00 for SCALE's real price); dashboard MRR then read $499.00 reconciled to ledger $499.00, matching (this repro doesn't itself show a live-vs-ledger divergence -- that is a separate, still-open hypothesis being tested next on a throwaway tenant, may be filed as a follow-up). All repro against approved test tenants only (test, e2e-routeflow).

title: MRR live-vs-ledger divergence: computeOverview()'s two queries filter differently -- a tenant billed then suspended leaves a permanent residue in ledgerMrr while live mrr correctly drops it
symptom: DB-verified reproduction (Lane F, 2026-09-18), exact live-vs-ledger divergence reproduced, not just the hypothesis. Root cause: computeOverview()'s two queries use different filters -- live MRR (payingWhere) gates on 4 conditions (planKey not null + tenant status=ACTIVE + deletedAt=null + class=PRODUCTION), ledger MRR (ledgerAgg, sums BillingEvent.amountDelta) gates on only 1 (tenant.class=PRODUCTION). A tenant billed once then moved off ACTIVE (suspended/cancelled) with no compensating event leaves a permanent residue in the ledger while live correctly drops. Exact repro on a throwaway qa-mrr-drift-test tenant (created, tested, then soft-deleted): resolved a real plan -> booked a +$499 BillingEvent -> baseline MRR $998/ledger $998 matched -> flipped status to SUSPENDED with zero new BillingEvent created (DB-verified) -> result: MRR $499.00 / 'Reconciled to ledger: $998.00 - differs by $499.00' -- the exact shape reported in prod, screenshot captured. Full writeup with exact API calls + DB queries + fix-shape options at local-assets/proofs/2026-09-18/mrr-ledger-drift-repro/REPRO.md in worktree rf-sweep-390. Severity critical: this is very likely prod's actual bug -- 26 tenants, some plausibly billed-then-suspended, meaning the platform dashboard's headline revenue figure may be silently wrong right now. Repro only on throwaway qa-mrr-drift-test tenant, created/tested/soft-deleted, per approved test-tenant policy.

title: No CAS on the Suspend direction in #926's compensating-delta fix -- two concurrent Suspend calls on the same tenant could each independently emit a compensating delta, double-counting the correction
symptom: Independent Opus review of PR #926: in the Suspend direction, 'before' is read and the compensating-delta decision made from that snapshot, but the actual write isn't gated on that snapshot still being current -- no compare-and-swap. Two concurrent Suspend calls on the same tenant could each independently emit a compensating delta (e.g. -$499), double-counting the correction in the ledger. title: Backdated inventory movements silently corrupt Product.averageCost and rewrite movement history -- recomputeProductInTx's replay is blind to raw order decrements, misstates valuation/COGS, and destroys its own audit trail
location: apps/api/src/inventory (recomputeProductInTx, called from recordPurchase/recordAdjustment on a backdated effectiveDate, and vendor-bill receive when billDate predates an existing movement); POST /inventory/recompute-costs (@Roles(OPERATOR) only, surfaced as a button in both the mobile warehouse tab and the web client); order creation/edit stock decrements that write no StockMovement row
symptom: Found incidentally during units/PO planning work, NOT part of that plan -- live production money bug, should be fixed well before any purchase-order edit work begins since that design depends on replay being trustworthy. Mechanism: recordPurchase/recordAdjustment called with a backdated effectiveDate, and vendor-bill receive with a billDate earlier than an existing movement, both call recomputeProductInTx. That replay starts stock at 0 and is BLIND TO RAW ORDER DECREMENTS -- order creation and edits decrement stock without writing a StockMovement row. So the replay computes a sales-blind average, overwrites Product.averageCost with it, and rewrites every stockAfter value -- erasing the very evidence that would let anyone detect or reconstruct the true figure afterwards. Severity critical/money: misstates inventory valuation and therefore COGS. Already-corrupted products are NOT recoverable from the ledger, which is what makes this worse than an ordinary arithmetic bug -- the corruption destroys its own audit trail. Same shape one layer down as the B523-family verification-gate problem (a check/replay that reports a confident number while structurally unable to see half the inputs) -- see also B556/B557 (same mrr/inventory-adjacent subsystem family, live-vs-recorded-state divergence from an incomplete view of writes). MUST go through bug-pipeline on its own merits and be fixed BEFORE any purchase-order edit work begins.

title: post-deploy-check has NO platform-admin/super-admin surface coverage -- it only authenticates as a tenant operator, so it structurally cannot verify anything behind SUPER_ADMIN auth
location: scripts/post-deploy-check.mjs (authenticates only as SMOKE_OPERATOR_USERNAME/PASSWORD against the e2e-routeflow tenant)
symptom: Found during tonight's #926 close-out: post-deploy-check.mjs authenticates only as a tenant OPERATOR (SMOKE_OPERATOR_USERNAME/PASSWORD against the e2e-routeflow tenant) and therefore structurally cannot verify anything behind SUPER_ADMIN auth -- including the exact platform-dashboard MRR reconciliation (mrr vs ledgerMrr) this whole day's B556/B557 work was about. Closing out #926, neither the fleet lead nor the landing coordinator could run that specific check from a session, not because a script is missing but because putting live super-admin credentials into an agent session is correctly the owner's call, never something sessions should arrange between themselves. Same shape as several findings filed today (B540/B559 overflow-detection blind spots, lessons L-202/L-205 -- assertions/checks that don't test what they claim): a gate that reports green while structurally unable to see an entire class of regression, here anything platform-admin/super-admin-only. Tooling/process gap, not a live bug. Recommended fix shape, either: (a) a SEPARATE post-deploy check tier gated on an explicit opt-in with owner-provisioned super-admin credentials (never defaulted/hardcoded), run only when someone with that authorization triggers it; or (b) at minimum, post-deploy-check's own output should say plainly 'platform-admin surface NOT checked' rather than reporting unqualified success, so a green run is never mistaken for full coverage.

title: ScanInvoiceModal submit composition raisesPo = inv.raisePo && !raisePoBlocker(...) has no test
symptom: raisePoBlocker is unit-tested (apps/web/lib/raise-po.test.ts) but the composition in the ScanInvoiceModal submit — raisesPo = inv.raisePo && !raisePoBlocker(inv.supplierId, billItems), sent as createPurchaseOrder: raisesPo ? true : undefined — has no test. Fix: extract shouldRaisePo(inv, billItems) into apps/web/lib/raise-po.ts beside raisePoBlocker, call it at the submit site, and add four jest cases: ON + unmatched line -> false; ON + no supplier -> false; ON + all matched -> true; OFF -> false. title: Mobile draft resume drops unitLabel: a Case line parked on web resumes on mobile as a pack line (288 pieces become 1, $480 becomes $42)
location: apps/mobile/lib/drafts-payload.ts (fromOrderDraftPayload / DraftCatalogLine); apps/mobile/components/NewOrderScreen.tsx (draft submit); mirrors apps/web/lib/drafts.ts DraftLineItem
symptom: With flag.units_v1 on, staff can sell an order line by a unit on WEB (CreateOrderModal, #1147). A parked web draft stores the line as unit 'Case', qty 1 (a count of the unit), unitPrice 480, unitLabel 'Case', no unitsPerBox. Mobile's fromOrderDraftPayload maps line fields ONE BY ONE and never carries unitLabel, so the same user resuming that draft on mobile gets a plain catalog line (draftSummary shows $480) that submits { productId, qty: 1 } with no unitLabel and no unitPrice: the server takes the PACK branch and stores 1 pack at the pack tier price ($42). A Case of 288 pieces silently becomes 1 and $480 becomes $42. ZERO exposure while flag.units_v1 is OFF for every tenant. Fix: mobile carries unitLabel through DraftCatalogLine and the submit payload, or REFUSES a draft containing a unit line (never degrades it to a pack line); add a web<->mobile parity test for the draft line shape. HARD GATE: this must be closed before flag.units_v1 is granted to any REAL tenant (it does not block the test-tenant flip); fleet lead ruling 2026-09-21, gates G6-G8. Found by the author-side Opus refute-first pass on #1147; web half (declaring unitLabel/packBase on DraftLineItem) is in the #1147 follow-up commit; mobile lane owns this.

title: Reversal keyed on free-text reference: a vendor bill number can delete or zero unrelated stock lots and movements
symptom: reverseBillLots finds lots with stockLot.findMany({ where: { reference: billNumber } }) — no productId and no source scoping — then deletes them or sets remainingQty 0. reference is free text also written by recordPurchase and recordAdjustment (default 'ADJUSTMENT'), and billNumber is user-typed, so unreceiving or voiding a bill whose number equals another flow's reference removes those lots tenant-wide (every default adjustment lot for 'ADJUSTMENT', a PO's receive lots for a PO number). Same shape: stockMovement.deleteMany on (productId, reference: billNumber, PURCHASE) at :1207 and on RET-<id8> at returns.service.ts:893. Changes FIFO/LIFO cost layers and the ledger; creates no stock or money. Unproven by a DB test.

title: Stock-count idempotency is keyed on a free-text movement reference: a planted STOCK_COUNT-<uuid> makes a commit a silent no-op
symptom: Both stock-count commit paths treat any existing stockMovement whose reference is STOCK_COUNT-<sessionId> as proof the count already committed and return alreadyCommitted without applying items. recordAdjustment.reference is user free text, so a movement written with that reference before the commit suppresses the count. No privilege gain (the same operator can adjust stock directly), so latent. Unproven by a DB test.

title: Invoice edit page re-saves a unit line as a pack line: a draft with 3 Cases stores 72 pieces instead of 864 and the money still reads $1,440, so nothing looks wrong
location: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/[id]/edit/page.tsx (load mapping ~:412-440 and save payload); apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts update() (pack branch); web InvoiceItem type has no unitLabel
symptom: With flag.units_v1 on, a DRAFT invoice can hold a line sold by a unit (created by POST /invoices with unitLabel, #1140, or copied from a New-sale order): stored as unitLabel 'Case', boxes 3, pieces 0, unitsPerBox 288, qty 864, unitPrice 480 (per Case), subtotal 1440. The invoice EDIT page maps that loaded item into its own line state keeping unitsPerBox and boxes but NEVER unitLabel (the web InvoiceItem type does not carry it). On save it derives boxes 3 / pieces 0 and PATCHes with no unitLabel; update() takes the PACK branch, which re-reads the PRODUCT's unitsPerBox (24): the line is stored as 3 boxes of 24 = 72 pieces at 480 per box = still $1,440. The unit label is lost and the stored quantity is 72 pieces instead of 864: inventory and the ledger silently lose 792 pieces while the money and every screen stay self-consistent, so no one sees it until a stock count. WORSE than the money-visible sibling defects (a $480 Case becoming a $42 pack shows as wrong money; B638 shows a wrong price) because the money still adds up. ZERO exposure while flag.units_v1 is OFF (no unit line can exist); this gates granting the flag to a REAL tenant, not the test-tenant flip. Fix (fail closed, fleet lead standing rule: wherever the server refuses a unit line the UI must refuse visibly, never convert, never fall back to the pack, never drop the unit): the edit page refuses to open a draft that holds a unit line, with a visible specific message; update() already refuses a unit request (4c-2 skipped). Also found the same class in the detail page label (3 Cases shown as '3 boxes'). Sibling defects the same night: A1 replaceAll re-denominating a Case to the pack, B638 mobile draft resume, invoice update() refusal becoming a silent conversion. Found while scoping units 5c (#938).

title: A missing git hooks directory is a silent no-op: pushes and verify report green while the pre-push gate never ran
location: core.hooksPath=.husky/_ (husky prepare) / worktree setup; guard scripts/check-git-hooks.mjs
symptom: husky sets core.hooksPath=.husky/_ (relative, shared repo config) and its prepare script creates that directory. A worktree made with npm ci --ignore-scripts (or any setup that skips prepare) inherits the setting but has no .husky/_, and git treats a hooksPath at a missing directory as no hooks: silently, exit 0. Every push from such a tree skipped the pre-push verify while looking like a push that passed it; found 2026-09-21 on the Mac lane-B worktree, and a sweep of the PC found 23 more worktrees in the same state (U-po x3, U-bugs, laneC, S-b638, coord-detached), all restored. CI ran on every merge and was the binding gate. Referenced as B637 in the 2026-09-21 session transcript. Companion finding: the force-push/checkout guard.mjs is a per-user PC-only PreToolUse hook (C:\Users\nakram\.claude\hooks), absent on every Mac session, so its absence also looked like success. Fixed by scripts/check-git-hooks.mjs: a fail-closed check wired into npm run verify and a silent-when-healthy SessionStart diagnostic, never into a lifecycle script (Docker builds run prepare with no .git).

title: Driver short-pick is not unit-aware: it steps in PIECES with no unitLabel/boxLabel handling, so a driver who delivers 3 Cases and types 3 records 3 pieces, not 36
symptom: Read-only from code on tree a6b3910a (master 6844c295 + #982 + #1121); NEVER SEEN RUNNING. apps/mobile/app/(driver)/route/stop/[stopId]/short-pick.tsx is an integer stepper in PIECES (its own comment: orderedQty and the qty steppers below are in PIECES), shows Ordered {qty} / Delivered [n], is capped at Number(li.qty), and has no unitLabel/boxLabel handling at all. routes/delivery-lines.util.ts accepts a delivered quantity anywhere in [0, ordered qty] with no unit awareness. Consequence: for a line sold as 3 Cases (qty 36 pieces) a driver who delivers 3 Cases and types 3 records 3 pieces instead of 36, a 12x under-delivery entered in good faith, feeding the delivery progress line and plausibly invoicing and returns. Exposure is zero while flag.units_v1 is off; it gates a real-tenant grant. Found by the Mac F2 prover while fixturing the #1121 proof (state C3'). Filed as a bug entry only, no fix.

title: Estimate to invoice to edit draft bills a boxed line 12x: convert drops boxes/pieces/unitsPerBox and the invoice edit page re-prices per piece
symptom: estimates.service.ts convertToInvoice creates the invoice line from only description, productId, qty, unitPrice, discount, taxRate, subtotal, msrp: it drops boxes, pieces and unitsPerBox. The invoice edit page hydrates isBoxSplit = it.boxes != null (false for the converted line) and sends {qty, unitPrice} without boxes/pieces, so the server update() prices per piece: an estimate line of 72 boxes of 12 ($20 per box, subtotal $1,440, qty 864 pieces) becomes $20 x 864 = $17,280 on Save; the form shows that total before Save. No spec pins boxes on convert. ROOT-CAUSE NOTE (shared by B641/B644/B645/B646): anywhere a line is reconstructed from {qty, unitPrice} without carrying boxes/pieces (and unitsPerBox), money or quantity is wrong by unitsPerBox. There are three independent reconstruction sites: Duplicate (B644), estimate convert (B645) and recurring invoices (B646), all predating units. All flag.units_v1 OFF, i.e. live today. Code-read by R-ui's sweep and verified again by the lead and the Mac Lead on origin/master; NEVER RUN.

ROOT-CAUSE NOTE (shared by B641/B644/B645/B646): anywhere a line is reconstructed from {qty, unitPrice} without carrying boxes/pieces (and unitsPerBox), money or quantity is wrong by unitsPerBox. There are three independent reconstruction sites: Duplicate (B644), estimate convert (B645) and recurring invoices (B646), all predating units. All flag.units_v1 OFF, i.e. live today. Code-read by R-ui's sweep and verified again by the lead and the Mac Lead on origin/master; NEVER RUN.

title: Standing-order generated orders never decrement stock but cancel credits it back
symptom: order-templates.service.ts creates the generated order via prisma.forTenant().order.create (status PENDING) and has zero stock references, while OrdersService.create() calls decrementStockForSale for non-draft orders. NOTE: R-ui traced only the CANCEL leg end to end. The edit-down, PENDING to DRAFT demotion and reopen legs are the sweeper's claim, NOT verified. Code-read only, verified again by the lead and the Mac Lead on origin/master; NEVER RUN; flag.units_v1 is not involved (live today).

title: Driver read surface omits unitLabel, so a driver's client cannot tell a Case line
symptom: RUN_LINE_ITEMS_SELECT omits unitLabel, so the driver run read carries no unit and the driver's client cannot tell a Case line from a pack line; this is the root cause of the driver short-pick problem in B643 (the stepper counts pieces). HOW KNOWN: sweeper x2 (two independent read-only sweepers agree); NOT verified by R-ui. title: Buyer cart merge path navigates to the order the client assumed, not the id the server returned
symptom: HARDENING, not a defect today. On the merge path (willMerge = !forceNew && activeOrder != null, ~line 54) handlePlaceOrder awaits createOrder.mutateAsync and then does router.push to orders/${activeOrder.id} (~183-184): the order the client ASSUMED its items would land in, not the id the server returned in result. title: Roll to next delivery of a CHANGE_QTY increase on a box-split line creates a DRAFT order 12x too big
symptom: For CHANGE_QTY, approveNextDelivery computes delta = Number(payload.newQty) - Number(li.qty) (~312), both in PIECES for a box-split line (the sibling APPLY_NOW branch feeds newQty to normalizeBoxesPieces({ qty: newQty, unitsPerBox }), orders.service.ts ~5333). It then calls ordersService.create({ items: [{ productId, qty: delta }], status: "DRAFT" }, buyerPseudoUser) (~355-357) with a BARE qty and the pseudo-user typed BUYER, where a bare qty counts SELLING UNITS (REG-B47; the buyer.controller.ts comment says 'never loose pieces — create() stores such a line box-unaware and bills qty x the BOX price'). Example: 6 boxes of 12 (qty 72) changed to 96 pieces gives delta 24, which becomes 24 BOXES at $40 = $960 instead of 2 boxes = $80. The stock decrement runs on the same wrong quantity when the draft is promoted (orders.service.ts ~2695). ADD_ITEM drops payload.boxes/pieces the same way (the spec pins items: [{productId, qty: 3}]). Precondition: an at-door or customer CHANGE_QTY increase on a boxed line resolved NEXT_DELIVERY. The result is a DRAFT, and the unit fence covers Case (unit-aware) lines only. THE CODE COMMENT THAT NAMES THE ROOT CAUSE, verbatim, change-requests.service.ts lines ~309-311: // units_v1: the delta is in the line's own unit axis but is re-created through create() as   // pack selling units at the live price — wrong for a unit-aware line.   unitAware.assertNoUnitAwareLines([li], "rolled to the next delivery"); The hazard was documented accurately and fenced for the unit-aware case only; the identical problem for an ordinary box-split line sat in the same three lines, unguarded. title: A short or refused delivery closed on account leaves the invoice at the FULL ordered quantity: the delivered-basis reconcile never runs when the payment amount is 0
location: apps/api/src/routes/routes.service.ts completeWithPayment (~2556-2625; guard :2607); apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts recordDeliveryPaymentInTx (early return :5079; reconcile calls :5126, :5135); apps/api/src/routes/routes.controller.ts (~200-209); apps/mobile short-pick.tsx (~143), payment.tsx (~332)
symptom: THE DRIVER MAKES A COMMITMENT AND THE SOFTWARE BREAKS IT. The driver tells the customer 'short, see office invoice for final' (mobile short-pick.tsx ~143, sweeper claim) and the system then sends an invoice for the full ordered quantity, including refused lines: over-billing after promising a correction, to a customer told to expect one. Every other defect tonight is a machine being wrong in private; this one has a person making a commitment on our behalf that the software then breaks (the lead). WRONG AGAINST ITS OWN DOCUMENTED INTENT: routes.controller.ts ~203-207 says every mobile completion, including $0 'on account', flows through this endpoint 'for its delivered-basis invoice reconcile', and that completions with no payment (or amount 0) must keep working. Yet completeWithPayment (routes.service.ts ~2556-2625) calls recordDeliveryPaymentInTx only behind 'if (dto.payment && dto.payment.amount > 0)' (:2607), and recordDeliveryPaymentInTx itself returns immediately on '!(amount > 0)' (invoices.service.ts:5079). The delivered-basis rebuild (reconcileOrderDeliveredInvoices, :5135, or rebuildIssuedDepositMirrorOnDelivery for an issued deposit mirror, :5126) is called at exactly one place, inside recordDeliveryPaymentInTx; R-ui's grep of the whole API finds no other delivered-basis reconcile caller (the filer's grep of origin/master agrees: the only non-definition call sites are :5126 and :5135). completeWithPayment writes deliveredQty per line (REFUSED forces 0) and flips orders to DELIVERED via a direct order.updateMany, so changeStatus's DELIVERED logic does not run. The code's own comment says on-account sends amount 0 (:5081-5083); mobile sends no payment when the method is 'Account' or the tenant lacks the driver_payments addon (payment.tsx ~332, sweeper claim). EFFECT: the DRAFT mirror stays at the FULL ordered quantity including refused lines while the order reads DELIVERED and deliveredQty says less; it over-bills unless an office user edits the draft. MITIGATION: it is a DRAFT; no office screen was found that surfaces deliveredQty beyond a line-status badge (R-ui did not check). HOW KNOWN: R-ui verified, the Mac Lead re-confirmed the gating lines on origin/master (:2607, :5079, the controller comment), the filer re-read the same lines and the call-site list; code-read only, NEVER RUN. Flag OFF, ordinary lines, live today. FIX-SHAPE NOTE FOR THE RECORD (not a fix): the reconcile does not belong behind a payment guard at all; lifting it out so it runs on every completion is a contained restructure; recordDeliveryPaymentInTx does payment work and calling it with amount 0 is not obviously safe. PROD DATA QUESTION 13 (owner batch): how many tenants close deliveries on account with no payment, and how many of those had a short or refused line versus their delivered-basis invoice totals. Sweeper claims I1-I5 stay UNFILED (I2, the customer's DELIVERED notification quoting the pre-short total, is the one to re-read first). Severity HIGH as ruled by the lead.

title: Web new-invoice form stores a product with unitsPerBox = 1 as a $0, qty 0 line
symptom: Chain: the product DTO validates unitsPerBox with @IsInt and no minimum, and inline edit saves any integer, so a product can carry unitsPerBox = 1. The web new-invoice form's addProductFromCatalog (~:863-865) reads 'product.unitsPerBox ? Number(product.unitsPerBox) : undefined' (1 is truthy), so it seeds boxes 1 / pieces 0, and :1081 and :1246 send boxes/pieces. On the server, manual-invoice-lines.ts (~52-66) guards on 'product?.unitsPerBox' (1 passes) and calls normalizeBoxesPieces WITHOUT qty; packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts:74 has 'hasBoxPackaging = upb > 1', so for upb 1 the helper returns qty 0. The line is stored with qty 0 and $0, and there is no zero-qty guard. Mobile and the web edit hydrate are guarded with '> 1'; the new-invoice form is not. It is the kind of defect discovered by an accountant, not a user. PRECONDITION: a product with unitsPerBox = 1. Whether any exists is a PROD data question: count active products with unitsPerBox = 1, then invoice items with qty = 0 and a productId on non-void invoices. FIX SHAPE (not a fix): one line in the form (treat upb <= 1 as no packaging) plus a spec that posts a unitsPerBox = 1 product through the form builder and asserts qty > 0; a server-side zero-qty guard is a separate call. HOW KNOWN: R-ui code-read; the Mac Lead confirmed the pricing rule (pricing.ts:74) and the form seed; the filer re-read the form line (:865), the server guard and the pricing rule on origin/master; NEVER RUN. Severity HIGH as ruled by the lead.

title: Standard returns of box-unaware lines restock BOXES as pieces (12x too few)
symptom: returns-restock.util.ts (~31-46) adds the RAW ReturnItem.qty to currentStock and to the stockMovement (quantity: qty; stockAfter: currentStock.add(qty)); the Mac Lead read it and the filer re-read it on origin/master. STANDARD returns store what the operator typed, in the order line's OWN unit (pieces for a box-aware line, BOXES for a box-unaware one), and returns-pieces.util.ts claims 'OrderItem.qty is ALWAYS stored as total PIECES', which is false for box-unaware lines (see B647 and B658). So restocking a box-unaware return adds boxes to a stock counted in pieces: 12x too few. UNVERIFIED UPSTREAM PREMISE, stated exactly: that the operator/returns UI types the return in the line's own stored unit for a box-unaware line is R-ui's trace, NOT run; if the UI converts to pieces first this defect does not occur on the standard path. Related: B660 (the ledger side, inline path only). Severity: the lead said MEDIUM-HIGH; the tool has no in-between, so it is filed as medium and can be raised. HOW KNOWN: code-read only; NEVER RUN. Inventory quantity, not money directly; refunds and the regulated ledger are separate paths.

title: Batch import drops packSize: stock and averageCost are wrong by the pack size for boxed lines
location: apps/api/src/import/batch-import.service.ts postBatch (:410; bill-line rebuild ~424-431); apps/api/src/vendor-bills/vendor-bills.service.ts lineInventoryDelta (:141-153), scan prompt (:1799)
symptom: postBatch rebuilds each bill line as { productId, name, description, qty, unitCost } and DROPS packSize (also sku and lineTotal), although the scan prompt asks for it (vendor-bills.service.ts:1799: 'packSize: units per box/case/pack as a number ONLY when the line explicitly shows one'), the extracted line type carries it (batch-import.service.ts:28), and extractedPayload keeps it (:213, :347). lineInventoryDelta (vendor-bills.service.ts:141-153) converts only when the line's OWN packSize > 1 (pack = item.packSize ?? 0) and never reads Product.unitsPerBox. WORKED EXAMPLE: 12 per box, 5 boxes at $24 printing '12x330ml', on hand 100 pieces at $2 per piece. Correct: +60 pieces, stock 160, averageCost $2.00. As coded: +5 pieces at $24 per piece, stock 105, averageCost $3.05. totalOwed is right; stock and the COGS basis are wrong. SECOND, SMALLER GAP: when the invoice prints no pack size the interactive flow lets the operator choose Boxes; the batch flow gives no way at all. NOT in code #1045 touches (it is web-only interactive-modal code). No import spec pins packSize (batch-import.service.spec.ts has no packSize). PROD DATA QUESTION: batch-imported vendor bills with a boxed product and packSize NULL, and their stock/averageCost deltas. Severity: the lead said MEDIUM-HIGH; the tool has no in-between, so it is filed as medium and can be raised. HOW KNOWN: R-ui end-to-end read; the Mac Lead re-confirmed the two decisive links (the postBatch line rebuild and lineInventoryDelta); the filer re-read :28, :213, :347, the postBatch map, lineInventoryDelta and :1799 on origin/master f05222b1; code-read only, NEVER RUN.

title: Editing, discounting or price-adjusting a DRAFT PARTIAL invoice cancels every order line that invoice does not bill, leaving those lines permanently un-invoiceable
location: apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts recomputeOrderFromInvoices (:2273-2420; orphan loop :2402-2414); callers :3540 (update), :3601 (discount/shipping), :6359 (applyPriceAdjustment); createPartialFromOrder
symptom: recomputeOrderFromInvoices ends with an orphan loop (~:2402): 'Order lines billed by no invoice: cancel (they weren't actually sold)', which sets status CANCELLED, qty 0, subtotal 0, boxes null, pieces null, invoicedQty 0 on every order line no non-void invoice bills, then rewrites the order total to the billed sum. Its docblock's design assumed whole-order coverage, but partial invoicing is a supported flow (POST /invoices/from-order/:orderId/partial, createPartialFromOrder, per-line invoicedQty). Callers: :3540 (update), :3601 (discount/shipping change) and :6359 (applyPriceAdjustment). The only guard is 'no non-void invoices: return' (:2284-2285). So editing, discounting or price-adjusting a DRAFT PARTIAL invoice cancels every order line that invoice does not bill: remaining = qty - invoicedQty becomes 0 and the line is CANCELLED with qty 0 and no stock return, so it can never be invoiced. No spec covers partial + recompute. Reachability is medium until the prod query runs (orders with at least one non-void invoice and a non-cancelled line with invoicedQty < qty). FIX SHAPE (NOT a fix): restrict the orphan cancel to invoicedQty = 0 AND a full-coverage precondition, or skip it when the order is partially invoiced. NOBODY IMPLEMENTS IT until a red-first DB spec exists; repro on test tenants only. HOW KNOWN: R-ui's trace; the orphan loop and the guard were re-read by the Mac Lead and again by the filer on origin/master f05222b1; code-read only, NEVER RUN. See the note on this record for the cancelled-line resurrection mechanism.

title: The global 'N parked drafts' tray covers page content at 768/390 (at 768 it covers the New-unit fields)
location: apps/web (global draft tray, responsive layout); component: web/global
symptom: The 'N parked drafts' tray at the bottom/edge of the page overlaps page content at 768px and 390px widths. At 768px it specifically covers the New-unit fields. Evidence: the #951 real-product Playwright VERDICT, states s5-partial-failure-768 and s3-three-levels-390. Fix approach not yet analysed; needs a z-index/positioning or collapse behaviour review at those breakpoints.

title: A CANCELLED order line still shows a delivery progress line
symptom: showDeliveryProgress && delivered != null && delivered < qty has no cancelled guard, so a CANCELLED line still shows e.g. '0 of 4 delivered' beside the CANCELLED status. Same on 28733b63:203 and #1121 be312d3f:213 — pre-existing, not a #1121 regression. Evidence: Mac VERDICT-M3b (c1121, 6 checks at 1440/768/390). Owner: S-order.

title: invoices.service.ts update() derives unitsPerBox from the LIVE product, not the line's stored snapshot
symptom: The SAVE path re-derives unitsPerBox from the live product record instead of the line's own stored snapshot, so a product repacked (unitsPerBox changed) after the sale re-prices an EXISTING line on the next save. Same class as the Senior Architect's ruling: a rewrite of an existing line must use its own snapshot; a null snapshot goes through legacyLinePieces and is refused on unknown. Found by S-order. Owner: U-units, to be folded into the buildLine conversion (W3).

title: returnedPiecesByProduct sums STANDARD line-unit qty and INLINE piece qty into one total
symptom: returnedPiecesByProduct adds STANDARD ReturnItem.qty (line-unit, ~126-129) and INLINE ReturnItem.qty (true pieces, ~131-133) into one result[productId], and the sum feeds the return cap at returns.service.ts:222 and inline-returns-quote.service.ts:187. Repro: a box-unaware line of 6 BOXES of a 12-pack (qty 6). A STANDARD return of 6 (all of it), then an INLINE return of 12 pieces, gives alreadyReturned = 18; either order hits 18 against a cap of either 6 (line unit) or 72 (pieces), so a whole return is wrongly refused or wrongly allowed. Fix: convert the STANDARD side to pieces through the shared line-pack-factors.ts / legacyLinePieces before summing. Found by Lane B. Owner: U-units, fixed with the classifier.

title: USB wedge-scan keydown effect tears down on every keystroke, so a real scanner never fires onScan
symptom: The wedge-scan keydown effect depends on [inputRef, onScan] and calls the onScan prop directly. Every consumer passes a fresh inline arrow, so each keystroke into a controlled input re-renders the parent, tears the listener down and resets the sequence; sequence.length >= 6 can never be reached, so a real wedge scanner never reaches onScan on any of the 12 consumers (inventory, invoices new/edit, products, vendor-bills, StockCountTab, ...). Every scan falls through to the field's manual Enter path instead. Pre-existing on master. The same file's camera path already uses onScanRef for exactly this reason. Becomes money-adjacent in #982, where the manual path consumes the typed Qty. Found by S-order with a deterministic RTL repro; fix PR coming. #982 stays not accepted until B672 lands and #982's wedge test asserts exactly +1.

title: approveNextDelivery ignores an ADD_ITEM change-request's boxes/pieces and creates the line from a bare qty
symptom: The ADD_ITEM change-request payload carries boxes/pieces, but approveNextDelivery ignores them and creates the next-delivery line from a bare qty. A boxed ADD_ITEM therefore lands as a selling-unit count instead of the boxed split — the same class as B655. Found by S-scan while fixing B655 (#1174). Owner: S-scan.

title: Invoice edit hydrates a legacy boxed line by falling back to the live product pack instead of the line's own split
symptom: A legacy boxed line (boxes non-null, unitsPerBox null — from pre-#1159 duplicates and historical estimate conversions) hydrates wrong on invoice edit in both clients. Mobile ((operator)/(tabs)/invoices/[id]/edit.tsx:123) has NO fallback: it withholds boxes/pieces and re-prices the line 12x on save. Web falls back to the LIVE product pack (it.unitsPerBox ?? it.product?.unitsPerBox), which the Senior Architect ruled out for existing lines. Fix for both: derive the pack exactly from the line's own split via packFromOwnSplit, never the live pack. Owner: S-order (mobile invoice edit), after B672. Found by R-ui.

title: 9 pre-existing *.db.spec.ts failures on a full local db lane run (estimates issue-date, order-number.db transaction timeout, cron-lock race)
symptom: S-order's full local db-lane run (npm run local:test:db) hit 9 pre-existing failures unrelated to their own change: an estimates issue-date test, an order-number.db transaction timeout, and a cron-lock race. Timeout and race could be load flakes from running the full suite concurrently rather than real defects -- needs isolated re-run per spec to confirm which are genuine before triage.

title: npm run local:test:db drops scoped test-name/path args before they reach jest
symptom: npm run local:test:db -- --testPathPattern <spec> silently runs the WHOLE db-spec lane instead of the one spec: npm's own -- separator stops the args reaching the wrapped jest invocation, and even when it does, this jest takes --testPathPatterns (plural), not --testPathPattern. Wastes time on every scoped debug run of the db-spec lane.

title: PO line cost stores per-piece cost at 4dp, losing cents at scale (11/box / 12 rounds to 0.9167, x1000 boxes = $11,000.40 not $11,000.00)
symptom: resolvePOLine (PO line create, U step 3) stores the per-piece unit cost rounded to 4 decimal places instead of carrying the box cost + pack size (or a higher-precision fraction) through to the total. $11/box / 12 units = $0.9167 (4dp), and 1,000 boxes at that rounded per-piece rate totals $11,000.40 on both the PO total and inventory value -- a real (if small-per-line) money drift that compounds at scale. Exposed by #1165's read-back (a 11.0004 per-box cost read-back). Senior Architect is ruling on the fix shape; carve-out: touches money, plan only, do not fix unattended.

title: AdminModal focus effect deps [open, onClose] steal focus to the close button on every keystroke in a controlled field (8/9 callers pass inline onClose)
location: apps/web components/AdminModal + callers, e.g. tenants/page.tsx:490-530 the delete-tenant confirm slug input, buyer add-link modal
symptom: AdminModal's focus-management effect depends on [open, onClose], and 8 of 9 callers pass a fresh inline onClose closure, so every keystroke in a controlled field inside an open modal re-renders the parent, re-creates onClose, re-runs the effect, and moves focus to the modal's close (x) button. In the tenant 'Permanently delete tenant?' confirm (slug input) and the buyer add-link modal, a keyboard user types one character and lands on the close button instead of continuing to type -- a real accessibility/usability defect, worse on a destructive-action confirm. The 4 existing AdminModal specs never re-render the parent while open, so this was never caught. Fix in flight (Lane B PR 2a: onClose moved to a ref, effect deps [open] only, repro-first spec). Related LOW findings from the same audit (dialog has no accessible name, close button is a bare x with no label, 4 error banners lack role=alert, 'Execute Merge' loses focus to body) -- not filed separately, tracked here for the same fix pass.

title: B661 sweep: six inline box-unaware qty x unitsPerBox piece derivations feed computeCategoryTax outside the ledger write point
location: apps/api/src/orders/line-piece-qty.ts; orders.service.ts ~2034 (create), ~3431 (re-price), ~3805 and ~4016 (edit paths); invoices.service.ts ~3442 and ~6253
symptom: Six inline box-unaware qty x unitsPerBox piece derivations feed computeCategoryTax's unitBasisQty outside the regulated ledger's own write point -- orders.service.ts (create ~2034, re-price ~3431, edit paths ~3805 and ~4016) and invoices.service.ts (~3442 and ~6253). Four of the six also set the line's own categoryTaxAmount snapshot directly. Each is an independent re-derivation of the same regulated tax basis quantity B661's fix already centralizes elsewhere -- the same 'one shared read/derivation, many independent copies' shape as B606 (L-210). Convert all six to @routeflow/pricing's regulatedUnitBasis and empty the guard allowlist B661's PR introduces (the allowlist exists specifically so these six show up as failures once the helper lands, not silently).

title: invoices.service.ts duplicate() copies items but writes no regulated ledger SALE rows for the copy -- a duplicated regulated invoice has no ledger footprint
symptom: duplicate() copies an invoice's line items (verbatim, boxes/pieces/unitsPerBox included per the earlier B644 fix) but never writes a RegulatedSalesLedger SALE row for any regulated-category line on the copy. The original invoice's SALE row exists; the duplicate silently has none, so the regulated ledger under-reports every duplicated regulated sale -- the tax/levy total the ledger is meant to reconcile against master data drifts low by exactly the duplicate's regulated lines.

title: SALE rows written before B661 still carry unitBasisQty as a box count for box-unaware lines; a piece-denominated return against them over-closes
location: RegulatedSalesLedger SALE rows written before B661's fix (regulated ledger, unfiled periods only)
symptom: Pre-B661 SALE rows carried unitBasisQty as a box count for box-unaware regulated lines, not the piece count B661's fix now writes going forward. A piece-denominated return against one of those old rows over-closes the regulated ledger (the return's basis and the sale's basis disagree by the pack size). Needs the owner-run, dry-run-first, id-pinned correction script the Senior Architect designed (same B662 shape: unfiled periods only, never touches a filed/closed period).

title: The strict line-ambiguity guard has no callers, so ambiguous boxed lines are never refused
symptom: buildLine, computeLineSubtotalStrict and AmbiguousLineError in packages/pricing exist specifically to refuse the shape "unitsPerBox > 1 with neither boxes nor pieces given" (the B644 shape). A repo-wide search across apps/api, apps/web and apps/mobile returns zero callers for any of them (confirmed via grep on 2026-09-22); build-line.ts's own doc comment concedes no API caller exists yet. Every real call site uses the lenient computeLineSubtotal, which has no ambiguity check and silently falls back to unitPrice * qty. The only live guard on this shape is regulatedUnitBasis, which only emits a logger.warn and only fires on the regulated-ledger path at write time. This is the root shape behind B644, B645, B655, B659, B661, B671 and B681 -- it is resolved by a different convention at each call site with nothing refusing it. Wiring the strict guard everywhere is the structural fix for the whole family; regulatedUnitBasis's own comment already anticipates being turned from a warn into a throw once buildLine is wired everywhere. Fast-follow, not release-blocking -- filed per the fleet lead's request during Release 1.

title: Comments describing the box-unaware fallback as qty-in-pieces contradict every writer, and cost real debugging time
location: packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts (and the related pieceQty naming in apps/api/src/invoices/manual-invoice-lines.ts)
symptom: pricing.ts:151 and :932 literally say the box-unaware fallback holds a qty 'in pieces' -- every writer of that fallback actually treats it as a box/selling-unit count, not a piece count. manual-invoice-lines.ts carries the same conceptual mismatch in its pieceQty naming/comments around the regulatedUnitBasis call site. These stale comments sent two engineers and the fleet lead to opposite conclusions on release night and cost roughly three hours. Correcting the comments (and pieceQty naming where it misleads) is a two-line-class fix with a disproportionate payoff -- fast-follow, not release-blocking. Filed per the fleet lead's request during Release 1; see B682 for the related dead-guard bug behind the same shape.

title: Scan-screen PriceEditor is a second priceHistoryEntry consumer and lacks the B606 unit guard
location: apps/web CreateOrderModal.tsx unit picker path + scan/PriceEditor.tsx
symptom: B606's fix (feat/u-picker-5b-r, #1147) guards CreateOrderModal's remembered-price display so a line priced by a unit (li.unitLabel set) never shows a pack-denominated priceHistoryEntry next to its price input -- showing a per-box remembered price beside a per-piece input is actively misleading. Master has since added a second, independent consumer of the same priceHistoryEntry data in the scan screen's PriceEditor (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/orders/_components/scan/PriceEditor.tsx), which has no equivalent unitLabel guard. Once the unit picker (#1147) and the scan-screen price editor coexist on master -- true for this release -- a unit-priced line reached through the scanner can display a pack-denominated remembered price. Surfaced by U-units while working #1147; explicitly out of scope for that PR per the fleet lead. Fast-follow, not release-blocking.

title: DB-lane specs (.db.spec.ts) carry no CI enforcement, so a fix guarded only by one is unprotected against regression
location: CI tooling -- all workflow files on master; DB-backed specs across the regulated/returns/money family
symptom: Verified across all six GitHub Actions workflow files on master: zero references to test:db, db.spec, or --db-specs -- the DB-backed jest lane never runs in any CI workflow. Demonstrated concretely on #1221 (Lane F's return-axis fix): with the fix reverted on a merged tree, all 395 unit tests in regulated and returns still pass, because the only real regression guard for that fix lives in a .db.spec.ts file that no CI job executes. This is not hypothetical for this one PR -- DB-backed specs are exactly what people reach for when a fix involves real transactions, so this is potentially a lot of the money-family work running genuinely unprotected against a future refactor silently deleting the fix, with every CI gate green. Not assumed to be an oversight -- CI may simply have no Postgres service, making the local-only DB lane a deliberate tradeoff -- but the consequence (unenforced regression guard) holds either way. Two candidate directions, neither chosen here: (1) give CI a Postgres service so the DB lane actually runs, or (2) make it policy that every fix carries at least one default-lane (non-DB) pin alongside its DB spec, so the regression guard exists somewhere CI executes. The existing repo idiom already solves the related problem and is the shape that works here: the copier-contract spec and the unit-line-writers AST scanner both fail the build when a new writer appears unregistered -- whatever direction is chosen should fail the build the same way, not merely document a convention. Third instance of this same class found in one release-night sweep (see B682 for the sibling dead-guard finding); filing now while the evidence is fresh rather than letting it be rediscovered later. Fast-follow, not release-blocking. Filed per the fleet lead's request during Release 1.

title: apps/api/tsconfig.json excludes prisma/** entirely, so seed.ts and its production-safety guards are never type-checked or linted
symptom: apps/api/tsconfig.json's exclude array contains prisma/** (alongside spec/test files, prisma.config.ts and scripts/**), so apps/api/prisma/seed.ts has never been type-checked or linted by the normal workspace commands -- not before this change and not after. Discovered by U-units while building #1223 (the units-flag seed grant): they had to type-check the file with a throwaway tsconfig override to verify their own change, and documented the gap in the commit/PR body rather than letting the next person rediscover it. The consequence is not cosmetic: seed.ts contains assertSafeTarget() and assertTestTenant() -- the guards that stop a seed script being pointed at a production database. A mistake in that file, including in the guards themselves, is caught by nothing automated (no tsc, no eslint). The exclusion may well be deliberate, since prisma/** also holds the generated Prisma client, so the likely fix direction is to type-check the hand-written scripts under prisma/ (seed.ts and any siblings) without pulling in generated output, rather than removing the exclusion wholesale. Fifth instance of the same pattern found in one release-night sweep alongside B682/B683/B684/B685: a control that exists, is believed to be working, and does not run on the thing it is supposed to protect. Fast-follow, not release-blocking. Filed per the fleet lead's request.

title: No test covers a return reversal and a credit-note reversal composing on the same order line
location: apps/api/src/regulated -- return-axis fix (#1221) x credit-note fix (#1219) composition
symptom: Both #1221 (return-axis fix) and #1219 (credit-note fix) are independently proven with red-first cases, and S-order's independent review confirmed the merge by content-identity against the true shared ancestors rather than by hunk count. But none of the six new tests across both PRs combines a return reversal and a credit-note reversal on the SAME order line. The reviewer accepted this as non-blocking on a structural argument: the per-order-line remaining aggregation is source-agnostic and additive, so the two reversal kinds net correctly by construction. That argument is sound, but it is verified by reading, not by execution -- the thing that would notice it ceasing to hold (a future refactor of the aggregation, for instance) is a test that does not exist. Fix direction: a DB-lane test (per B685, DB-lane tests are the right home for a real-transaction composition case like this) that books a sale, applies both a partial return AND a partial credit note against the same line, and asserts the aggregated remaining/regulated-filing figures are correct -- converting the accepted structural argument into an executable proof rather than leaving it as prose in a PR review. Filed as non-blocking per the reviewer and the fleet lead -- both #1221 and #1219 ship without it. Fast-follow, not release-blocking. Filed per the fleet lead's request.

title: apps/api spec/test files are excluded from type-checking, so a drifted fixture only fails at runtime and only if an assertion happens to touch the wrong field
symptom: apps/api/tsconfig.json:7 sets isolatedModules: true, which ts-jest inherits, making the Jest transform transpile-only; tsconfig.json:26 additionally excludes **/*.spec.ts and **/*.test.ts from the compile unit entirely. Result: 512 spec files on master are type-checked by NOTHING. A fixture that drifts from the type it models fails only as a wrong runtime value, and only if an assertion happens to touch that specific field -- Lane B hit exactly this during Release 1, a NaN where 4 was expected, because a fixture lacked a newly-required field. On a codebase whose fixtures encode money and regulated-filing quantities, the failure mode is a test that passes while silently asserting the wrong number. Ruled fix shape (Senior Architect, SA-056): a separate apps/api/tsconfig.spec.json extending the base tsconfig with exclude: [] and include: src/**/*.spec.ts, plus a check-types:spec script run alongside check-types in npm run verify; lands as a ratchet with a pinned allowlist of not-yet-passing files that only shrinks (same discipline as size-ratchet.spec.ts); standing rule that a fixture modelling a Prisma row is written with ; and this must NEVER be fixed by deleting tsconfig.json's exclude, because nest build shares that same tsconfig file and specs would land in dist. apps/api/tsconfig.plan-gate-specs.json (six files, nothing runs it) is the existing seed for the pattern. Sixth instance of the same class found in one release night (a control that exists, is believed to be working, and does not run on the thing it protects) -- and by surface area the largest: 512 files. Related to B686 (apps/api/tsconfig.json also excludes scripts/** and prisma/**, same shape, different exclude entry). Fast-follow, not release-blocking. Filed per the fleet lead's request, sourced from the Mac mini via SA-056.

title: PO cost edit on a RECEIVED PO's boxed line silently does not persist, closes the modal as if saved
symptom: On a RECEIVED PO's boxed line (12/box, cost $12/box), editing cost to $11/box, Save, then choosing 'Keep stock as is' on the re-apply-to-inventory prompt closes the modal as if the edit succeeded -- no toast, no error. A PATCH IS sent with the new shape (caseCost:11, cases:5, loosePieces:0), but a DB read-back shows PurchaseOrderItem.unitCost is still 1.0000 and totalCost still 60.00 -- the write silently did not persist. Re-opening the PO shows the stale $12. PO cost feeds inventory valuation, so this is a silent-money bug: the UI and the operator believe the cost was corrected, and nothing downstream is told otherwise. Found by Mac F2 during the Release 1 RC proof, confirmed by direct DB read-back on a test tenant -- symptom-only with DB evidence, cause not traced (F2 did not trace into the surface). Live in production since #1210 merged 10:30Z and deployed 10:32Z. Disposition: fast-follow, not release-blocking -- explicitly not fixed same-day per the lead's ruling (an untraced cause plus a ~90 minute gate is how #1207 got a defect into production this morning; not repeating that shape twice in one release).

title: Editing a DRAFT PO a second time is rejected by the API: an untouched boxed line round-trips malformed fields
symptom: A DRAFT PO edited once, re-opened, then edited again touching only a plain (non-boxed) line is rejected by the API with: 'items.1.property caseCost should not exist; items.1.property cases should not exist; items.1.property loosePieces should not exist; items.1.qtyOrdered must not be greater than 9999999'. Item 1 is the OTHER, untouched boxed line -- the client round-trips it back to the server carrying case-shape fields (caseCost/cases/loosePieces) it should not have, plus a malformed qtyOrdered value. The user sees a generic 'Couldn't update the purchase order.' and nothing partial lands -- the whole save is rejected, so this is a blocked-save bug rather than a silent-corruption one, but it is the same family as B689: an untouched line's state does not round-trip cleanly between the stored shape and the shape the client sends back on save. Found by Mac F2 during the Release 1 RC proof on a test tenant. Disposition: fast-follow, not release-blocking, per the lead's ruling alongside B689 -- untraced cause, not fixed same-day.

title: The bug-hunt dead-model-guard signature's write-pass regex cannot see a forTenant() write chain, so it flags actively-written models as never written
symptom: Meant to do: dead-model-guard flags a safety check reading a model nothing writes -- the B54 shape. Actually does: flags models that ARE written, whenever the write goes through an inline this.prisma.forTenant().model.create(...) chain, asserting with full confidence they are 'never written anywhere in apps/api.' Produced two false leads: userPreference and importQueueItem -- for the second, the writes are in the SAME FILE the scanner flags, at lines 127, 142, 218, 353, 400, 477 and 506, while it flags reads at 258, 421 and 525. Cause, one sentence: the write-pass regex at scan-signatures.mjs:1107, /\b[\w$)\]]+\.(\w+)\.(create|createMany|update|updateMany|upsert|delete|deleteMany)\s*\(/g, starts with \b, and there is no word boundary at the ) that ends forTenant() because the character before it is (, so the chain cannot anchor and is invisible to this pass. The read pass explicitly alternates (?:prisma|tx|forTenant\(\)) as its receiver and therefore sees the same models fine -- reads credited, writes not; that asymmetry is the whole defect. Why the self-test did not catch it: the signature's own clean fixture writes through an aliased client, db.fixtureLedger.create, with a comment saying that is the receiver shape the write pass actually credits -- the fixture encodes the limitation instead of testing it. Blast radius, measured: 67 models in apps/api are written via an inline forTenant() chain; 22 are written ONLY that way and are latent false leads the moment anything reads them, including regulatedFiling, tobaccoReport, trackedCategory and trackedSubcategory -- the compliance surface. Suggested fix: add forTenant\(\) to the write pass's receiver alternation as the read pass already has, or drop the leading \b; replace the clean fixture with the inline shape so the self-test proves the real case, with two of the 22 as regression fixtures. Verified by running the regex against the real files, not by reading it. This is the scanner relied on for pre-PR gating, and it has been quietly blind to the most common write shape in the codebase. Fast-follow, not release-blocking. Filed per the fleet lead's request, sourced from the MacBook lane.

title: Manually setting an order to DELIVERED/PARTIALLY_DELIVERED never writes deliveredQty, so office-marked deliveries cancel with full stock credit and every invoice voided
symptom: order-cancel-impact.ts:39-44,89 sums deliveredQty to decide cancel impact, but a manual changeStatus to DELIVERED (orders.service.ts:2634-2635) writes only deliveredAt, never deliveredQty -- only routes.service.ts's route-completion path (:2584, :3085) writes deliveredQty. Consequence: an order marked DELIVERED by staff in the office (not through a completed route stop) still reads deliveredQty=0, so cancelling it restores full stock and voids every invoice as if nothing was ever delivered -- B56's blanket-void gate (deliveredQty>0) never fires because the signal it reads was never written. Fix: manual DELIVERED writes deliveredQty=qty per active line; manual PARTIALLY_DELIVERED requires per-line quantities. Found by MacBook's A2 state-machine verifier (Fable, refute-first), pre-existing on master, not in today's train. Fast-follow.

title: unvoidInvoice never checks the owning order's status, so unvoiding a cancel-voided invoice yields a sendable invoice for a CANCELLED order

Unvoiding an invoice that was voided because its order was cancelled produces a live, sendable invoice attached to a CANCELLED order -- surfaced on both clients (web invoices/[id]/page.tsx:2265-2275, mobile invoices/[id].tsx:189-190,579). Fix: refuse unvoid when the order is CANCELLED. Found by MacBook's A2 state-machine verifier, pre-existing on master, fast-follow.

title: voidCreditNote never checks Return.creditNoteId, so a CN backing a REFUNDED return can be voided, stranding the return with no credit and no path back
symptom: credit-notes.service.ts:918-951 voidCreditNote never checks Return.creditNoteId. processRefund claims a return REFUNDED then mints the credit note ISSUED, so the CN is voidable immediately afterward; once voided, the return is stranded REFUNDED with no credit and no path back (cancel already refuses a REFUNDED return, :858-859). title: PO detail views re-derive line subtotals as qtyOrdered times unitCost instead of reading the stored totalCost, contradicting the store side one screen over
symptom: Web PurchaseOrdersTab.tsx:112 and mobile purchase-orders/[id].tsx:208 both re-derive a PO line's subtotal as qtyOrdered * unitCost (unrounded) instead of reading the stored, already-correct totalCost. #1199 (B677) fixed the STORE side only. title: A notes-only PO save silently rewrites a bill-raised line's exact stored total, because buildUpdateItems derives the split from the LIVE product pack instead of the line's own stored packSize
symptom: Confirmed by Mac Lead: saving a PO edit that touches only notes (no line changes) silently rewrites a bill-raised line's exact stored total (11,000.00 -> 11,000.40). Same root mechanism as B690 (now refuted as a repro artifact, but its code-read stands and is moved here): buildUpdateItems in purchase-orders-edit.ts sends the LIVE product pack as packSize and derives the split from it, ignoring the line's own stored packSize -- so ANY save, even a notes-only one, re-derives and can silently change a line's money even when the operator touched nothing about that line. SA-059's ruling attaches: an edit must derive from the line's OWN stored packSize; the live product pack is for NEW lines only. Silent stored-money change, not merely a display bug -- cross-link B690 for the DRAFT-double-edit symptom that shares this cause (that symptom itself did not reproduce on a fresh master API image and is refuted separately, but the underlying mechanism is real and lives here). Fast-follow.

title: pack-at-sale.ts reads the LIVE product.unitsPerBox even though invoices.service.ts snapshots unitsPerBox on every order-derived InvoiceItem, so a repack before delivery phantom-books quantity on the regulated filing
symptom: pack-at-sale.ts:19-23 reads the LIVE product.unitsPerBox, on the premise (stated in its own header) that only split lines are snapshotted -- that premise is FALSE: invoices.service.ts:955 snapshots unitsPerBox on EVERY order-derived InvoiceItem (finance.prisma:276-279, explicitly 'carried from the order line, never the live product'). Effect: after a repack (12->24) before delivery, delivered-basis reconcile reverses -60 and re-books +120 -- net +60 phantom pieces on the period's filing -- and a later full inline return reverses only $25 of a $50 line. SA-062 fix: packAtSale = it.unitsPerBox ?? packMap.get(it.productId) ?? null; rewrite the header (it's wrong about the snapshot premise); warn with invoiceItemId + both packs when snapshot and live differ (repack signal). Red-first cases: {qty 5, unitsPerBox 12, boxes null} with product now 24 must book 60 not 120 on BOTH create and resync; {unitsPerBox null, product 12} must still book 60. SA reads the diff before merge. High, own PR, fast-follow -- part of the live-pack-reinterpreting-a-stored-line class (see cross-linked siblings).

title: invoices.service.ts update() re-derives a stored box split at the product's LIVE unitsPerBox instead of using packFromOwnSplit, so any invoice save after a pack edit can halve the line and back-sync the corruption onto the order
symptom: invoices.service.ts update() re-derives a stored box split at the product's LIVE unitsPerBox. packFromOwnSplit exists for exactly this case ('never from the live product, which may have been repacked since') and has one caller in the whole repo, estimates.service.ts:472; siblings at invoices.service.ts:2334 and :826-836 already use it -- update() was missed. Fires on ANY invoice save after a unitsPerBox edit: products.service.ts:865-880 allows free pack edits with no draft-invoice check; the web sends boxes/pieces beside qty and normalizeBoxesPieces ignores qty when a split is present; the three upstream guards check unitLabel, which a pack change does not carry; update() calls assertInvoiceRewriteAllowed (unit-aware-guard.ts:143-175) which does not catch this shape either. The halved qty/invoicedQty back-syncs onto the ORDER line at :2346-2355, so the corruption escapes the invoice entirely. Fix: route update() through packFromOwnSplit like its siblings. Server-only surface. Fast-follow -- part of the live-pack-reinterpreting-a-stored-line class.

title: invoices.service.ts:3391 truthy check on unitsPerBox treats a pack-of-1 product as boxed and passes no qty, zeroing the line
symptom: invoices.service.ts:3391 reads if (product?.unitsPerBox), which is truthy at unitsPerBox===1 (a pack of one, i.e. sold individually -- the exact B664 shape) and on that branch passes no qty. A caller sending boxes on a pack-of-1 product zeroes the line. API/mobile-only -- the web client cannot reach this path. Fast-follow.

title: Sale-side stock decrement for a box-unaware line uses the box count against piece-denominated currentStock, under-decrementing by the pack size at every write site
symptom: create(), DRAFT->PENDING promote, and settleStockForEdit all decrement a box-unaware line in BOXES against piece-denominated currentStock (orders.service.ts:1980, :2125, :2219-2227, :2695-2698; order-stock.ts:82-95, :164-200) -- never expanded to pieces at any sha since b8446f03. currentStock is pieces by definition (SA-060, all sixteen writers except this one). #1217's piece-basis restock is the CORRECT side of this pair (confirmed by SA-060, no revert) -- after #1217 this under-decrement becomes visible as a net stock gain on return instead of silently self-cancelling as it did before. Fix: sale-side decrement/restore must route through the same pack resolver #1217 uses. Existing shortfalls in currentStock are repaired only by a post-count append-only adjustment (SA-029), not a backfill script. High, fast-follow, release-blocking family closed by #1217 but this sibling is the reason the old numbers were already wrong under the covers.

title: Standard-return refund omits tax and category tax, minting a lump-sum credit note that shorts the customer
symptom: returns.service.ts:619-712 priceReturn uses invItem.subtotal only. processRefund (:802-807) mints a lump-sum credit note at that subtotal-only amount. The inline return path correctly refunds subtotal+tax+categoryTax. Example: a line of 50 subtotal + 10 tax + 4 category tax -> standard-return CN is 50.00, customer is short 14.00. Fix shape pending SA (a CN-cap change). High, fast-follow.

title: Cancelling a return after its source invoice was voided leaves a positive filing residue that can never be cleared
symptom: returns.service.ts:876-880's cancel claim never reads invoice status. unreverseReturnEntries (regulated-ledger.service.ts:476-479) is a blind deleteMany; the inline path (:600-650) does the same. If the source invoice was voided (e.g. by a separate correction) before the return is cancelled, the deleteMany removes the wrong rows and leaves a positive residue on the filing permanently -- a second void attempt throws, so there is no self-heal path. Fix: unreverse up to the current net, or refuse cancel when the source invoice is VOID. High, fast-follow.

title: Unvoiding an invoice restores it with a fully reversed regulated ledger, since the ledger un-reversal has been deferred and untracked since #181
symptom: invoices.service.ts:4537-4555 unvoidInvoice flips the invoice back to DRAFT, but the ledger un-reversal was deferred since #181 (comment at :4546-4547) and never tracked since. resyncInvoiceLedger's preserveReturns (:161-163) keeps VOID-CN rows in the reconciliation, so a line billing 5 nets to 3 after an unvoid. Fix: unvoid should run resyncInvoiceLedger with preserveReturns limited to non-VOID returns/CNs. High, fast-follow.

title: Mobile order edit-items seeds unitsPerBox from the LIVE product instead of the line's own stored value, refusing every save of a unit line and silently re-denominating a repacked legacy line

Two failure modes: every mobile save of an order holding a unit line is refused with a 409 UNIT_AWARE_LINE (the line's own snapshot never reaches the request); and a repacked legacy split line is silently re-denominated at save (22.50 -> 21.25 in the observed case). Fifth instance of the live-pack-reinterpreting-a-stored-line class tonight (sibling of B657/B674, and of the pack-at-sale/notes-only-save/invoice-update() ids filed alongside this one). title: updateOrderItems prices and gates from a pre-lock snapshot, so a concurrent at-door commit and an operator edit interleave into stock, invoice and order figures that all disagree
symptom: orders.service.ts:3099-3105 reads the order OUTSIDE the transaction; :3268-3273 takes FOR UPDATE but heldItems feeds only assertHeld and settleStockForEdit. The diff branch resolves li from the STALE order.lineItems (:4306) and writes stale qty/unitPrice/boxes/promoFreeUnits (:4382-4530); the DELETE guard (:4137-4141) reads snapshot invoicedQty. Interleave: operator opens a price-only edit reading qty 2; driver at-door commits qty 5; operator saves, writing qty 2 and settleStockForEdit credits 3 back -- the van carries 5, order/invoice say 2, stock is +3 phantom. Arm B: createInvoiceFromOrder's bare orderItem.update of invoicedQty (invoices.service.ts:1293-1297, :2843-2848) races a concurrent DELETE reading snapshot invoicedQty 0 -> the line is hard-deleted, InvoiceItem.orderItemId SetNull. Fix: after the lock, tx.orderItem.findMany full columns and resolve li from THAT; fail closed on a missing payload id (same shape as B135's fix, :5290-5316). Found by MacBook's A5 concurrency verifier (Fable, refute-first). Tomorrow's first fix after the SA-063 family.

title: expireTrials races subscribe(), so a tenant subscribing during the sweep gets locked READ_ONLY by a stale bare update

title: Mobile invoices screen drops the customerId query param, so every link meant to filter invoices by customer lands on the unfiltered list

title: vendor-bills page's Bills and Purchasing ledger row has the same qty x unitCost fallback drift as B698

title: invoices.service.ts's pack branch charges the box price per piece on a partial-box line, and nulls the line's unitsPerBox snapshot in the same save
symptom: On an invoice DRAFT edit, a line with a partial box sends boxes:0 and pieces:N. invoices.service.ts:3400 enters its pack branch because 0 is not null; packFromOwnSplit returns null because it requires boxes > 0; unitsPerBox (declared :3389) stays undefined; computeLineSubtotal falls to its non-boxed branch and charges the BOX price per PIECE. Five loose pieces of an $11 twelve-pack save as $55.00 instead of $4.58 -- the multiplier is the pack size, so a 24-pack overcharges twenty-four fold. A notes-only save is enough to trigger it (no line edit required). Worse than the overcharge: the same save at :3457 writes unitsPerBox: boxes != null && unitsPerBox ? unitsPerBox : null, which stores null and destroys the line's pack snapshot -- and update() re-syncs the regulated ledger, so the wrong figure reaches a tax filing. Also affects box-unaware lines, not only partial-box ones. Live regression introduced by #1236 (merged 05782852, tonight), confirmed on origin/master directly by the fleet lead rather than relayed. Do NOT revert #1236 -- it fixed a real defect of its own and a revert reintroduces it. Fix-forward, being written now by the session that found it. CRITICAL, hotfix priority, ahead of everything else in tonight's queue.

A concurrent product substitution on the same line between context-build and lock-acquire throws, where the pre-B709 code path did not. title: Every timestamp on money tables is a naive DateTime, not timestamptz -- only one column in the whole schema is timezone-aware
location: apps/api/prisma/schema/*.prisma (every createdAt/updatedAt except platform.prisma:853); session-timezone-dependent comparisons and driver reads
symptom: RETRACTION of this id's original filing: the original 'invoice-line edit stamped ~3 hours ahead of the DB clock' finding was a misread, not a defect. InvoiceItem.updatedAt (apps/api/prisma/schema/finance.prisma) is a plain DateTime with no @db.Timestamptz, mapping to Postgres 'timestamp WITHOUT time zone'. node-postgres parses a naive timestamp as LOCAL time of the machine running the script (the owner's PC, UTC-5) and prints it with a trailing Z regardless -- a stored 18:47:51 displays as 23:47:51Z. now() is a real timestamptz and printed correctly. Comparing the two manufactured a 3-hour gap that does not exist. The REAL finding, now with hard evidence rather than a concern: exactly ONE column in the entire schema is timestamptz -- platform.prisma:853. Every other timestamp, including every createdAt/updatedAt on money tables, is naive. Two demonstrated consequences: (1) a query comparing a naive column against a timestamptz literal resolves using the session timezone -- B717's exposure query was correct only because that session happened to be UTC (confirmed directly: session_timezone = UTC), which nothing in the repo asserts or tests; (2) any tool reading these values over a driver shifts them by the reading machine's offset, demonstrated tonight at exactly the owner's PC's 5-hour offset (LOCALTIMESTAMP of 20:45:55 printed as 2026-09-23T01:45:55Z when the session was forced to UTC) -- the same shift that produced the original phantom 3-hour gap. A report can silently disagree with itself depending on who ran it. Suggested guard, not a prescribed fix: a spec asserting the session timezone, or @db.Timestamptz on the money tables -- both options named, neither chosen here.

title: The per-item order note never reaches the people who handle the goods -- it's absent from the packing list, dispatch manifest, driver checklist and invoice email
symptom: The per-item order note is absent from the aggregated packing list -- RUN_LINE_ITEMS_SELECT (routes.constants.ts:16-34) does not select it and the aggregation carries no note field; absent from the dispatch page's per-stop manifest, which renders only name and quantity; absent from the driver's delivery checklist ((driver)/route/stop/[stopId]/index.tsx:55-62); and absent from the invoice email body. The field's own placeholder promises it 'prints on invoice' -- it does, and reaches nothing else. Broken promise to the user: a note written to communicate something about an item (a substitution note, a handling instruction) never reaches the warehouse staff packing it, the dispatcher routing it, or the driver delivering it. Arguably the most valuable of a five-bug set from the same trace. Multi-line notes PR fixes this one; the other four are separate ids. Fast-follow.

Fast-follow.

Unreachable weight on a money-adjacent DTO. Fast-follow.
