title: The janitor's merged-worktree detection is wrong in both directions -- it can propose deleting a live prover's tree, and it under-removes genuinely merged branches because it uses ancestry on a squash-merge repo
symptom: Two independent failure directions from the same root cause: merged-detection decides 'merged' by ancestry (is the branch head an ancestor of origin/master), which is the wrong test on a repository that squash-merges everything. Direction 1 (over-removal, found first tonight): a merged-and-clean worktree with a live prover process rooted in it still got ranked among the top reclaim actions -- git calls the tree clean, but nothing checks for a process cwd'd inside it. It also only enumerated routeflow-clean's worktrees, so a live tree in the routeflow checkout was safe by accident. Passing --target made the planner reach for the biggest object rather than the safest, widening eligibility rather than just ranking within it. Direction 2 (under-removal, found later, more damaging because it's silent): because this repo squash-merges, a landed branch's head is NEVER an ancestor of master post-merge, so the ancestry check is effectively dead for the common case. Seven worktrees were protected as 'branch not merged' including rf-lane-b707, whose PR #1245 merged hours ago at f10bf3b5 and whose branch is already deleted from origin. Fix for both directions: drop ancestry entirely. Query the pull request's actual state via the GitHub API, or compare tree/content, never commit ancestry -- the same remedy in both directions, and the same trap the inline-returns mobile lane will hit when it rebases after #1250 squashes onto master (its branch head will also never be an ancestor). Guard for direction 1: before proposing 'remove whole worktree', require no process cwd inside the tree, no recent mtime inside, no keep-marker, and enumerate every checkout on the box, not just one. A --target size parameter must rank among already-eligible actions and never widen eligibility. Report-only (the current default) is why direction 1 never actually deleted anything -- that discipline is why report-only should stay the default until both directions are fixed. With 30.6 GB free tonight there is no pressure to apply anything.

title: Consider moving return-key minting out of the shared @routeflow/returns package
location: packages/returns (mintReturnKey, once the feat/extract-returns-logic-package PR lands)
symptom: The extraction package carries mintReturnKey — generates a fresh identifier per capture attempt, web's model. Mobile does not use it: an offline-queued submission must reproduce the same identifier on replay, so mobile derives a persisted key in its own module instead. Both platforms already pass the key into the shared code as a plain parameter, so the package never needs to own generation at all. It was kept in the shared package for this PR only because the extraction was a strict pure move (zero insertion/deletion) and deleting the function would have made that move unverifiable. Design point, not a defect: evaluate removing minting from the shared package (receive a key, never produce one), with web's call site moving to its own module the way mobile's already has. No user-visible effect at present. Credited to the review that raised it; the lane was right to keep it as-is for this PR.

title: Inline-returns capture screen shows unconditional success even when the ledger reversal was parked
location: apps/api/src/returns/inline-returns.service.ts:93 (reverseLedgerForReturn, returns void) called from capture() line 310; apps/web inline-returns capture dialog (#1250)
symptom: The inline-returns capture screen (#1250) displays a return number, credit note and refund amount on every successful capture. Underneath, capture() calls reverseLedgerForReturn(), which the B681 park guard (#1255, merged same batch) can now silently PARK instead of reversing when the row's basis can't be safely determined -- the function returns void, and the only signal is a server-side warning log. Neither the capture response type nor the dialog carries any notion of a park, so an operator completing a return has no way to know one happened. The money itself is not wrong -- parking is money-safe by design, that is the point of the guard -- but parked rows accumulate invisibly and surface only much later when a period filing is blocked (see B681), at which point whoever investigates has far less context than at the moment of capture. Neither #1250 nor #1255 introduced this gap alone; it exists only because both landed in the same batch, which is exactly what an individual PR review cannot see. Suggested shape (from the finder, not prescribed): carry a parked count/flag through the capture response and surface it in the dialog.

title: SA-078(b) fix (#1257) is pinned by query-shape test for only 1 of 4 rebuildSiblingDrafts callers -- the other 3 are structurally blind to a lost select
location: apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.reconcile-pack.spec.ts (new); the 4 rebuildSiblingDrafts callers: reconcileOrderDeliveredInvoices:1611, rebuildIssuedDepositMirrorOnDelivery:1718, resyncOrderInvoicesForEdit:2017, reconcileSplitOrderDrafts:2165
symptom: #1257 fixed the 4th caller (rebuildIssuedDepositMirrorOnDelivery) never selecting {orderItemId, unitsPerBox} on its items query, which left the carried pack empty for prepaid/deposit-mirror orders. The new spec file has exactly one query-shape assertion (queryArgs.select.items toEqual {select:{orderItemId:true, unitsPerBox:true}}), and it targets ONLY the just-fixed 4th caller. The other three callers are covered only by output-value assertions (e.g. createdItem.unitsPerBox === 12) against a mocked prisma.invoice.findMany that returns whatever the fixture says regardless of the real select clause -- structurally blind to a lost select, the exact shape of gap #1257 just closed for caller #4. resyncOrderInvoicesForEdit and reconcileSplitOrderDrafts have NO SA-078(b) coverage at all (grepped every .spec.ts referencing either name). Not a defect in shipped code -- verified correct and complete for all four callers by direct trace -- but a real regression-coverage gap: if a future edit strips unitsPerBox from the select on any of the other three, nothing in the current suite would fail. Fix shape (from the reviewer, stated explicitly so nobody re-derives 3 more copies of the same blind test style): ONE spec that greps every caller of the shared rebuildSiblingDrafts core and asserts each one's own items-query select carries both {orderItemId, unitsPerBox}, count-pinned at 4 callers -- so a 5th caller added later without the select fails the build rather than passing silently, rather than writing 3 more per-caller tests that would inherit the same blindness style being replaced.

title: Web order-create Case/Unit toggle is display-only -- never creates a unit-aware line, so per-unit pricing cannot be entered

symptom: Owner-reported: cannot set a price per unit when selling by unit. A case at $12.59 for 15 units derives $0.84/unit, but the product actually sells at $1.29/unit, and there is no way to enter that. The money math for exactly this case is built, tested and live behind the units flag -- ProductUnit (catalog.prisma:313-341) carries an explicit price plus 4 tier prices per level, not just a conversion factor; resolveUnitPrice (packages/pricing/src/unit-levels.ts:186-203) already prefers an explicit level price and only falls back to division when one is absent; buildUnitLine (apps/orders/unit-line-build.ts:256-281) already accepts a staff-typed price and classifies it as a discount below list or an upsell above list. Only the surface is missing: the web Case/Unit toggle sends no unitLabel and the code comment states outright that the price is unchanged either way because proration is linear -- the toggle changes how a quantity reads, never what is charged. The single editable field remains the case price. See B737 for the missing unit-price-configuration screen this depends on.

title: Scan tray shows the pack price instead of the unit price for a unit-sold cart line -- same defect #1264 fixes elsewhere, unreached by that fix
location: apps/mobile/lib/scan-tray.ts#trayRowsFrom; caller apps/mobile/app/(operator)/orders/NewOrderScreen.tsx:~1351 (priceFor callback calls tierPriceFor directly, no unitPriceBase/unitLabel awareness); latent sibling at apps/mobile/lib/edit-items-draft.ts#draftTrayRows
symptom: Found during #1264's review as the live 4th consumer that PR's own fix (lineUnitFor/CartRow priceBase) doesn't reach. trayRowsFrom iterates the ENTIRE cart every time the barcode-scan camera modal opens (gated on scanOpen, NewOrderScreen.tsx:2459) -- routine operator behavior, not an edge case. Its catalogRow() computes each row's subtotal via computeLineSubtotal, but the caller's priceFor callback supplies tierPriceFor(product) directly with zero unit-price awareness (TrayLine/TrayProduct don't even carry a unitLabel field). Traced the arithmetic: for a unit-sold line with no manual override, computeLineSubtotal takes the boxes==null&&pieces==null branch and returns unitPrice(pack tier price) * qty(case count) -- e.g. $24 x 1 = $24, while the cart row and footer correctly show $220. Opening the scan camera with a Case line already in the cart shows the wrong price in the tray beneath it. Fix (from the finder): route scan-tray.ts's priceFor callback through unitPriceBase/the line's own unitBasePrice, same shape as the fix #1264 already applies to lineUnitFor/CartRow -- small, mechanical. Also check edit-items-draft.ts#draftTrayRows's priceFor while touching this: it reads a stored catalogPrice field that is ALSO wrong for a hydrated unit-sold line (hydrateFromOrder sets catalogPrice = product.pricePerUnit, never unitPriceBase) but is currently latent, not live, because catalogRow's ternary prefers line.unitPrice whenever set and a hydrated line's unitPrice is always the server's real stored price -- cover both call sites of trayRowsFrom in one pass rather than leaving the latent one for a fifth discovery.

title: VendorBillsService.revertToDraft DELETES PURCHASE StockMovement rows instead of appending a reversal
Live return path books a legacy-shaped row's box count as pieces when the product was un-boxed after the sale (classifier fail-open)
location: packages/pricing/src/legacy-box-axis.ts (classifySaleAxis productPackNow gate) via regulated-ledger.service.ts bookReversalChunk; returns.service.ts receive() / inline capture()
symptom: SA-173 (board issue #2052): on the LIVE return path a legacy-shaped SALE row (qty equals unitBasisQty, box-unaware) on a product whose box size was removed after the sale is indistinguishable from a genuinely piece-axis row of a never-boxed product, so classifySaleAxis reads it non-boxed-now and the reversal books the box count as pieces. Fail-open on the regulated ledger, LIVE-NOW. Evidence that separates the two shapes: a linked source split, the SA-161 SALE-ledger ratio (unitBasisQty / qty integer > 1 for B661-written rows) or product pack-change history. The fix is in the resolver, own tier-1 read. The resolution walk (#1324, SA-173) already uses the operator-attested pack; the live path does not.

title: Standard receive() never takes the Order lock before reverseReturnEntries, so two concurrent receives on one order race
symptom: Opus W/N on #1324: the STANDARD receive() path calls reverseReturnEntries without the Order row lock the live create/capture/cancel paths and the parked-reversal resolution take (Return -> Order). reverseReturnEntries reads per-line remaining balances then books, so two concurrent receives (or a receive racing an inline capture) on one order can both read the same remaining and over-reverse the regulated ledger. Returns lane, medium.

title: Partial invoice: the same order line twice in one request skips the remaining-quantity check (over-bills a line)
symptom: Board #2069 (found by the Opus pass on #2061). The remaining-quantity check runs per request item against the stored invoicedQty, so two entries for the same orderItemId in one request are each checked against the same remaining amount. A line with 96 remaining at 10/unit (960) and a request of [X 60, X 60] passes both checks and bills 120 pieces (1200). Fix: refuse duplicate orderItemIds (400) or aggregate before the check, red-first spec.

title: Partial invoice: concurrent partials can over-bill (remaining check outside the transaction, unconditional invoicedQty increment)
symptom: Board #2070 (found by the Opus pass on #2061). The remaining quantity is read before the transaction and the invoicedQty increment is unconditional, so two operators billing the last 96 pieces at once both pass and invoicedQty ends at 192 on a 96-piece line. Fix: make the check and increment atomic (conditional update in the transaction or a row lock on the order line; never a second in-process lock), with a DB-lane concurrency spec that fails on the old code.

title: Web new-invoice preview shows qty x unitPrice for boxed lines (subtotal not passed)
symptom: Board #2071 (found by the Opus pass on #2061), display only. The preview does not pass the line subtotal, so it falls back to qty x unitPrice: a boxed Case line worth 960 previews as 11520. Fix: compute each line through @routeflow/pricing computeLineSubtotal like the saved invoice, red-first test and 390/768/1440 captures.

title: Invoice prefix and payment-due days in Settings → Invoicing never save
symptom: The Invoicing tab sends invoicePrefix and paymentDueDays to PATCH /settings, but neither field is in the allowlist or returned by GET, so both blank on reload. Real numbering lives in /import/numbering; no tenant-level default payment terms exist (customers carry their own). Found while writing the onboarding playbook (TEN-M9 in docs/product/tenancy.md).

title: Business name can't be changed after a workspace is created — the tenant's edit is silently discarded and the back office shows it read-only
symptom: Business profile shows required Business Name / Account Email inputs, but PATCH /settings excludes both ('NOT editable by tenant admin'), so edits vanish with no error. The back-office Configuration tab shows businessName read-only and UpdateTenantConfigDto has no businessName, so no screen can correct a misspelled name after creation (TEN-M8).

title: New drivers get no invite email — their temporary password must be passed on by hand
symptom: DriversService.create() mints a temporary password and returns it in the API response but sends nothing; staff created via POST /users/operator get a set-password invite (sendSetPasswordInvite), drivers do not. Onboarding has to relay each driver's password in person.

title: Back-office welcome email sends the new tenant admin a plaintext temporary password
symptom: createTenant's welcome email embeds the admin's temporary password in the message body (forcePasswordChange applies only when it was auto-generated). The staff path already uses a hashed, expiring set-password link (UsersService.sendSetPasswordInvite); the tenant-admin path should too. The same email uses trial wording, which misreads for sales-led paid customers (documented in the onboarding playbook).

title: Create-tenant form can't set the trial length — the API accepts 1–90 days, the form always uses the 14-day default
symptom: CreateTenantDto.trialLengthDays (1-90) exists but the six-field back-office form has no control for it, so every sales-created workspace gets TRIAL_LENGTH_DAYS=14 and goes READ_ONLY via expireTrials if payment isn't recorded in time.

title: Back-office Manual Activation and Change Plan offer only STARTER / PROFESSIONAL (=SCALE) / ENTERPRISE — a GROWTH customer paying by bank can't be activated on GROWTH
location: apps/web/app/(platform-admin)/admin/tenants/[id]/page.tsx:98 PLANS (used at :521 change plan, :941 Manual Activation)
symptom: The tenant detail page hardcodes PLANS = [STARTER, PROFESSIONAL, ENTERPRISE]. planKeyFromEnum maps PROFESSIONAL to SCALE, so GROWTH (a public tier) and LITE are unselectable in both the plan control and the Manual Activation form, although the API accepts them (SELECTABLE_TENANT_PLANS). A bank/Zelle/check payer on GROWTH can only be activated on the wrong plan (wrong entitlements and MRR). The create form is catalog-driven and unaffected.

title: Product CSV import reads only name, price, description, unit and SKU — pack size, tier prices, barcode, category, cost and tobacco-flag columns are silently ignored
symptom: Only Item Name/Name, Rate/Sales Rate/Price, Description, Unit/Usage Unit and SKU are read; unitsPerBox, priceTier2-5, barcode, category, standardCost/averageCost, isTobacco, msrp and reorder columns are dropped with no warning, and re-import matches by name and skips existing rows so it can't fill them later. A richer JSON path (POST /products/import: barcode, category, opening stock, averageCost) exists but its hook useImportProducts has no call site; the Move-to-RouteFlow page forwards only name/sku/price/unit/category. White-glove onboarding must hand-enter pack sizes and tiers per product.

title: Customer CSV import never sets payment terms, price tier, credit limit, tax-exempt status, tax ID or tobacco licence — those columns are silently ignored
symptom: The contacts importer reads names, phones, email, billing/shipping addresses (+ optional lat/lng) and currency only; defaultPaymentTerms, pricingTier, creditLimit, isTaxExempt, taxId, tobaccoLicenseNo/Expiry, delivery window and consent are never read, so they must be set customer by customer. It also does not geocode: addresses without Latitude/Longitude columns import with no coordinates.

title: Supplier CSV import has no screen — POST /import/expense-suppliers is only reachable through a hook nothing calls
symptom: The supplier importer exists server-side but useImportExpenseSuppliers has no call site in apps/web, and the Import page says suppliers are auto-created from expense vendor names. Onboarding a wholesaler's supplier list therefore means adding each supplier by hand.

title: Numbering card promises 'continue where your old system left off', but live invoices, estimates and credit notes ignore it and mint INV-<year>-#### from defaults
location: apps/api/src/import/numbering.service.ts mintForYear (~300-360) vs updateSettings year:0 (~124-150) · settings/import NumberingCard (page.tsx ~495)
symptom: Since B100/F16b, reserveNext for INVOICE/ESTIMATE/CREDIT_NOTE uses a per-tenant-year series that lazy-seeds from built-in DEFAULTS (INV-/EST-/CN-, pad 4) and the tenant's own <PREFIX>-<year>-#### documents; the year-0 row the Numbering card writes (prefix, next number, padding) is never read on that path, and seedFromSource has no callers. A migrating wholesaler who sets 'next invoice 10543' still gets INV-2026-0001, and the card's preview shows a number live minting will never produce. Either the card drives the per-year series or its copy stops promising continuity.

title: Settings → User management 'Add User' ignores the Role picker — choosing Driver creates an Operator (office) account
location: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx AddUser modal (~435-443, Role select ~517-524) · apps/web/lib/api/users.ts useCreateOperator · apps/api/src/users/users.service.ts:187
symptom: The Add User modal offers Role: Driver / Operator, but onSubmit never sends role, useCreateOperator also drops name, and createOperator hardcodes role OPERATOR. Anyone added as a 'Driver' here gets an office account with operator access instead; drivers must be created from Drivers → New Driver. The staff member's display name is also discarded.

title: A 365-day manual (bank/Zelle/check/cash) activation is stored as a MONTHLY billing cycle, so after the first period it rolls forward one month at a time
symptom: activateManualSubscription writes periodEnd = now + billingPeriodDays but never sets TenantSubscription.cycle, so the schema default MONTHLY stays even for a 365-day payment; rollCycles then advances such a period by +1 month once it lapses. Proven by REG-ROLL-MANUAL-ANNUAL and a local end-to-end run (2026-09-25 billing QA), and present on a live production tenant (read-only report).

title: Setting a custom price on a tenant that isn't paying yet (e.g. TRIAL) books the price into the MRR ledger, so ledgerMrr runs ahead of MRR
symptom: When planKey is set and basePriceSnapshot is null, updateTenantPriceOverride backfills the snapshot AND emits PLAN_CHANGED +monthly without the paying-set check (isPayingRow), so a TRIAL tenant is booked into the ledger before it pays. Local run: +1,200 ledger on a TRIAL Enterprise tenant with MRR unchanged; pinned by REG-OVERRIDE-BACKFILL-TRIAL.

title: A back-office add-on granted with a Stripe price is charged in Stripe but never enters MRR (no priceSnapshot, no BillingEvent)
symptom: The admin enableAddon path creates a real Stripe subscription item when a stripePriceId is given, but never writes TenantAddon.priceSnapshot or emits a BillingEvent, so MrrService and the ledger never see the charge (the tenant self-serve path does both). Pinned by REG-ADMIN-ADDON-MRR; production has no such rows today (latent).

title: Billing overview's per-plan baseMrr subtracts discounts but the top-level baseMrr does not, so the two figures disagree
symptom: Top-level baseMrr accumulates base (no discount) while byPlan[plan].baseMrr accumulates base - discount; with one fully discounted SCALE tenant and one SCALE annual tenant the page shows baseMrr counting both and byPlan SCALE counting one. Found by REG-MRR-ANNUAL (2026-09-25 billing QA).

title: Approved test workspaces (test, e2e-routeflow, qa-lite, routeflow-demo, ux-audit-*) are class PRODUCTION in production, so they count in platform MRR and tenant stats
symptom: Read-only production report (2026-09-25): every one of these approved test slugs has class PRODUCTION, so MrrService's PRODUCTION-scoped numbers include them. The platform MRR of $99 comes entirely from the 'test' workspace's manual activation; real customers contribute $0 of it. routeflow-demo should be DEMO and the qa-/e2e-/ux-audit- slugs TEST per tenant-class.ts.

title: Cancelling a subscription clears a downgrade the tenant had scheduled, so after resuming they stay on (and are billed for) the higher plan — needs an owner ruling
symptom: Local end-to-end run (2026-09-25 billing QA, step 9): after scheduling GROWTH→STARTER, cancel() itself nulls downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt; resume() then leaves the tenant on GROWTH with no downgrade, so the next cycle bills 249 instead of the 99 the tenant chose. The B216 ruling protects a tenant-chosen downgrade from admin/webhook paths; whether the tenant's own cancel should also preserve it (and resume restore it) is an owner call.

title: Annual subscribers count at the full monthly list price in MRR; owner ruled MRR = annual price ÷ 12
symptom: OWNER RULING 2026-09-25: an annual subscriber counts annual ÷ 12 in MRR (Scale annual $4,990 → $415.83/mo). Today the checkout webhook and subscribe() write basePriceSnapshot = catalog MONTHLY price regardless of cycle and book +monthly into the ledger, so annual customers show 20% high (annual = monthly × 10). Pinned today by REG-MRR-ANNUAL / REG-WEBHOOK-ANNUAL-SNAPSHOT on test/billing-qa; those pins must flip. Decide with the SA whether to store the annual-equivalent snapshot or divide at report time, and how to restate existing annual rows.

title: routes.service completeWithPayment/completeStop return {} to callers: cached idempotency replay is typed unknown
symptom: checkIdempotencyKey() returns Promise<unknown>, and both methods do 'if (cached) return cached;'. The truthy-narrowed unknown is {}, which widens each method's inferred return type to {}, so every caller loses the typed response. routes.service.spec.ts:2000 reads response.paymentIds and fails to type-check (TS2339 'paymentIds' does not exist on type {}); it is the one error left in #1315's check-types.spec baseline for that file. Runtime is unaffected: the replay returns the saved response object. Fix shape: type the cache read (checkIdempotencyKey<T>, or cast the replay to the method's own response type) and annotate the return type, so a replay and a fresh call share one declared shape.

title: A SKIPPED stop accepts a replayed offline completion (201)
symptom: A driver's queued offline completion replays after the office marks the stop SKIPPED, and the 201 silently applies onto a terminal stop.

title: Driver route list stays stale after the offline queue drains
symptom: After a completion replays and lands, the mobile route list keeps showing the stop as Up next / 0 Done until a manual refresh.

title: A skip can overwrite a just-committed COMPLETED stop (check-then-update race)
symptom: A skip that reads PENDING just before a completion commits overwrites COMPLETED with SKIPPED, stranding the delivery side effects.

title: DRIVER changeStatus has no assignment check (any tenant driver can confirm any PENDING order)
symptom: The DRIVER role branch of changeStatus confirms any PENDING order in the tenant with no stop-run assignment check; change-request resolve uses a different, narrower predicate.

title: merge-duplicate-products/merge-pending-orders/import-zoho dial raw DATABASE_URL, no local-only guard
symptom: Three prod-capable scripts connect with the raw DATABASE_URL string and have no local-only allow-list check, unlike the shared localConnectionConfig guard from #2419.

title: NSF fee line still taxed by mobile invoice edit + B294 backfill
symptom: hydratedLineTax infers a diluted rate from the header subtotal (which includes the NSF fee) and fills it onto the NSF line as taxable during a DRAFT mobile edit; the B294 backfill script has the same gap.

title: POST /credit-notes/:id/apply with no invoiceId returns 500 instead of 400
symptom: The apply DTO does not validate invoiceId, so a missing value reaches the service and throws an unhandled 500.

title: Typed line price snaps back to ladder after 'Not available' to undo (picker remount refresh)
symptom: Marking a units_v1 tiered-product Case line 'Not available' then undoing unmounts/remounts the price picker; its first-sight tier refresh silently reverts a typed STANDARD price back to the ladder price.

title: next/font Google build-time fetch fails deploys intermittently
symptom: next/font/google fetches fonts at build time; a transient Google Fonts fetch failure fails the whole web build, blocking a landing twice in two days.

title: upgrade()'s optimistic CAS guard omits priceOverrideMonthly, letting a price change race it
symptom: A concurrent Pricing change to a subscription's negotiated fee can race a plan upgrade: the upgrade's optimistic guard matches only on tenantId+planKey, not priceOverrideMonthly, so it can silently apply the upgrade's basePriceSnapshot over a fee that changed underneath it. (GitHub #2470)

title: Payment-failed email embeds a short-lived Stripe billing-portal bearer URL
symptom: The payment-failed notification email links directly to a just-created Stripe billing-portal session URL, a short-lived bearer link — by the time the recipient reads the email the session is often expired, and until then the link grants portal access to anyone holding it. (GitHub #2473)

title: Import status sweep's CAS keys on status only, leaving an ABA gap under concurrent writes
symptom: The end-of-import invoice status sweep compare-and-sets each row on {id, status} only; a status that changes away and back to the same value between the sweep's read and its update is invisible to the CAS, so a concurrent write in that window can be silently overwritten with no reported count. (GitHub #2471)

title: Standalone multi-invoice payment can deadlock (40P01) with no retry
symptom: recordStandalonePayment locks its invoices FOR UPDATE in id-sorted order while completeWithPayment locks them in delivery order; the resulting lock-order conflict can be detected by Postgres as a deadlock (40P01), failing the payment request outright with no automatic retry. (GitHub #2472)

title: Order cancel and invoice write-off derive their decisions from unlocked pre-reads
symptom: Order cancellation decides whether to credit stock back (cancelReturnsStock) from an order snapshot read before the cancel's own row lock is taken, and invoice write-off reads the invoice's status via an unlocked findOneOrThrow before writing WRITTEN_OFF unconditionally — both can act on a value a concurrent write has since changed. (GitHub #2472)

title: recordPayment doesn't refuse a WRITTEN_OFF invoice, unlike its payment-recording siblings
symptom: recordPayment refuses only a VOID invoice, while recordStandalonePayment and the bookkeeping payment path also refuse WRITTEN_OFF via the shared paymentRefusal helper — so a payment can still be recorded against a written-off invoice through this one entry point. (GitHub #2472)

title: A null reissue read-back after issuing a return credit falls back to the stale pre-issue snapshot
symptom: When re-reading a return after issueCredit() unexpectedly returns null, the code falls back to the pre-issue snapshot instead of treating the read as unknown/retryable, so the caller can get back stale credit-note/hold state for a return that just changed. (GitHub #2477)

title: Order-embedded inline-return capture discards parked reversals instead of surfacing them
symptom: applyInlineReturnInTx returns only out.minted from captureAndIssueInTx and discards any parked-reversal result, so an order-embedded inline return never reports a parked reversal to its caller, unlike the standalone inline-return capture path which surfaces it via withParkedReversals. (GitHub #2477)

title: No client lets an operator approve or resolve a parked reversal
location: apps/mobile (returns flow — no parkedReversals handling); apps/web/app/(dashboard)/returns/_components/RecordInlineReturnDialog.tsx (displays parkedReversals as read-only text; file's own comment notes 'No held/approve/reject UI')
symptom: A parked reversal (stock not taken off the order because delivered pieces exceeded a cap) is invisible on mobile, and on web is shown as read-only text with no action to approve or resolve it — operators have no way to clear a parked reversal from either client. (GitHub #2477)

title: Mobile buyer edit-items hydrates seller-added custom lines as 'Product' and sends them as productId null
symptom: hydrateBuyerDraft keys the draft on li.productId with no custom/unlisted skip; a staff-added custom line (productId null, product null) shows as 'Product' and rides Save's replace plan as {productId: null}; buyer DTOs have @IsString productId, so Save likely 400s or drops the staff line. Web golden skips them (orders/[id]/page.tsx:575, li.productId && li.product) with 'Custom items added by the seller aren't listed here'. Runtime unconfirmed; the fix must also prove whether the server's buyer replace preserves a custom line absent from the plan.

title: Web invoice edit at 390px: the line grid overflows, so Tax % and delete are clipped and unreachable
location: apps/web invoice edit page, line-item grid (inside an overflow-x-hidden main)
symptom: At a 390px viewport the invoice-edit line grid renders ~428px wide inside a ~294px column; main is overflow-x-hidden, so descriptions collapse and the Tax % cell and the delete button are clipped and cannot be reached. Pre-existing (found by F2 during the #2673 captures, #2554 5876471892). Owners and staff use the web on phones. Fix: a responsive line layout at 390/768; Playwright 390/768/1440.

title: Web InlineReturnSection gives every line's Qty input the same id, so the labels point to line 1 and later lines are unlabelled
symptom: Every line's Qty input renders id="qty-(pieces)"; both <label htmlFor> point to line 1's input, and line 2+ inputs have no accessible label; clicking a later line's label focuses line 1. Pre-existing; found by F2 during the #2712 captures (#2554 5877344670). Fix: a per-line unique id (e.g. by line key) + an RTL pin getByLabelText per line.

title: skip-verify audit log records the checked-out HEAD, not the pushed ref
symptom: On 2026-09-28 a SKIP_VERIFY push of a non-checked-out branch (feat/2696c-special-override @65a745b8) was logged in skip-verify.log as the checked-out branch/sha (feat/2715-pr1-edit-scanner-card | 72710173); the audit records the wrong ref (#2554 5877642450). Fix: read the pushed refs from the pre-push stdin (`<local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>` per line) and log each; a fixture test that pushes a non-HEAD branch.

title: pre-push trunk-push refusal reads HEAD, so pushing a non-HEAD ref to master is not blocked
location: .husky/pre-push (the trunk check ~:43-45 uses git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
symptom: The hook refuses a push only when the CHECKED-OUT branch is main/master; `git push origin feature:master` from any other branch passes the local guard. GitHub branch protection and rulesets are NOT available on this private repo (the API returns 403 'Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public'), so the local hook is the only trunk guard while private. Fix: reuse B892's pre-push stdin parse (RF_PUSH_REFS) and refuse if ANY remote ref is refs/heads/master or refs/heads/main; a fixture test pushing feature:master is refused.

title: prorateLineSubtotal is non-monotone on BUY_N_GET_M box-split lines: a larger delivered qty can bill LESS
location: packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts:384 prorateLineSubtotal (callers: returns/inline-returns-pricing.ts:274, regulated/regulated-ledger.service.ts:102, mobile returns-logic.ts:275, short-pick.ts:403,523,640)
symptom: With freeUnits>0 and freeUnitSize>1 (box-split line stored with a promo snapshot) the floored free-unit telescope makes the curve drop: stored 24.00, 20 pcs, 2 free boxes of 4 - 9 pieces bills 18.00 but 10 pieces bills 12.00. Built through applyBestPromotion -> computeLineSubtotal: 297 of 648 swept lines (upb 2..12, BUY1GET1/2GET1/1GET2/3GET1) have at least one delivered qty that bills less than a smaller one, e.g. upb2 BUY1GET1 8 pcs stored 40: 3 delivered bills 30, 4 bills 20. Partial credits/returns/price-correction targets computed from it are wrong by up to one box price. Found by SA-574 characterization (test tenants only).

title: The invoice's delivered-basis bill (prorateLineSubtotal / buildInvoiceItemData telescope) is non-monotone: more pieces delivered can bill less
location: packages/pricing/src/pricing.ts:384 prorateLineSubtotal + apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:836-885 buildInvoiceItemData (same floored free-unit telescope)
symptom: Related to B894 (not the same fix). A free unit is a whole selling unit (a box) on a pieces axis, so no whole-free-unit allocation is monotone point by point: stored 24.00, 20 pcs, 2 free boxes of 4 - 9 pieces bills 18.00 but 10 pieces bills 12.00; a later partial delivery can be a NEGATIVE invoice line although the sum still equals the stored subtotal. Customer-visible on partial-delivery invoices. Fixing it needs free allocation in PIECES on invoice lines (promoFreeUnits axis, computeLineSubtotal contract, DRAFT round-trip, reconcile's sum-of-free-units mirror) and changes customer bills, so it is owner-visible: a plan and an owner yes come before any build. Do not fix inside B894.

title: lint:migrations (Squawk) does not refuse SET LOCAL without an explicit BEGIN/COMMIT
symptom: Prisma does not wrap these migrations in a transaction, so a migration that uses SET LOCAL outside an explicit BEGIN/COMMIT runs it as a silent no-op (the setting never applies to the statements after it). npm run lint:migrations passes such a migration. The guard should fail a migration that contains SET LOCAL with no enclosing BEGIN/COMMIT. Source: SA-582, board #2554. Tooling.

title: pre-push and verify let a commit add a cache dir (.jest-cache/, ~2,400 files, ~38 MB) that .gitignore does not cover
symptom: A commit reviewed in #2742 added 2,401 .jest-cache/ files (about 38 MB of source maps carrying a local absolute path) and nothing refused it: .jest-cache/ is not in .gitignore and the pre-push chain has no size or cache-dir check. The guard should (1) ignore .jest-cache/ and (2) refuse a push that adds files under cache or build directories, and any push adding more than N MB. Source: #2742 review, board #2554 comment 5884288517. Tooling.

title: inventory assignToVariants runs a Serializable transaction with no retry, so a concurrent family edit can surface a raw 40001/P2034
symptom: On master, assignToVariants runs its transaction at isolationLevel Serializable (timeout 60s) with no retryOnTxConflict wrapper. A concurrent edit to the same product family can abort it with a serialization failure (Postgres 40001 / Prisma P2034), and that raw error reaches the user instead of a retry. Fix: wrap the transaction in retryOnTxConflict. Fixed by #2741 (M2); close this bug when #2741 lands. Source: SA-587e, board #2554 comment 5885586130.

title: wipe-tenant-fresh-start.js NUKE_MODELS misses six models and mis-orders two, so a tenant with those rows fails the wipe (P2003)
symptom: NUKE_MODELS has no entry for CommissionAccrual, CommissionPayout, CustomerCommissionRate, AgentAssignment, SupplierProduct or SupplierCredit, so deleting the parent rows of a tenant that has any of them fails with a foreign-key violation (P2003). It also orders returnRecord after order and payment after transaction, so those deletes hit their referencing rows first. Separately, reset-and-seed.ts names Prisma delegates that no longer exist. Fix: add the six models before their parents, reorder the two, drop the dead delegates, and add a spec that walks the schema so a new tenant-scoped model cannot be missed. Test tenants only. Source: SA-594, board #2554 comment 5887915534. Tooling.

title: inline-returns-quote labels TIER vs BASE with tierForProduct > 1, which differs from !== 1 on a null or 0 tier; route it through isSpecialTier
symptom: The quote service picks the TIER-versus-BASE price label with `tierForProduct > 1`, where tierForProduct = tierByProduct.get(productId) ?? customer.pricingTier (line 371). The shared rule elsewhere is `!== 1`, and the two disagree on a null or 0 tier: `> 1` reads it as BASE, `!== 1` reads it as a special tier. The null/0-tier semantics must be decided (owner/lead call), then the label routed through isSpecialTier from @routeflow/pricing so there is one definition. Until then it is allow-listed in #2751's no-mirrors pin. Source: SA-588c, board #2554 comment 5893065870. Money-adjacent (price label); test tenants only.

title: iOS: the price-edit modal (LinePriceModal) never appears from the scan tray while the scan sheet is open; it queues behind ScanOrderSheet's Modal
symptom: iOS: the price-edit modal (LinePriceModal / Edit price) never appears from the scan tray while the scan sheet is open; it queues behind ScanOrderSheet's Modal and shows only after Done. Pre-existing on master 2a27877f; affects standard and special lines. Repro: New order, pick a customer, add a line, open the scan sheet (camera denied is fine), press the line's price pencil. It makes #2751's special-price override unreachable from the scan tray on iOS. The fix is owner-ruled: old native screen versus the hybrid shell. Source: U-units, board #2554 comment 5893110537.

title: the picker tap AND scan should both honour ProductUnit.isDefaultSelling (web addLineItem, mobile acceptScannedProduct); web unit-options defaultUnitValue is unused
location: apps/web addLineItem (orders/estimates/expenses/StandingOrderModal); apps/mobile acceptScannedProduct; apps/web/lib/unit-options.ts defaultUnitValue
symptom: Follow-up to SA-580. A product's default selling level (ProductUnit.isDefaultSelling) is not applied consistently: the picker tap and a barcode scan should both start a new line at that level, but web addLineItem and mobile acceptScannedProduct do not both honour it. web/lib/unit-options.ts exports defaultUnitValue(product, options), which returns the default level's value, yet nothing in the web app calls it (only its own test does), so the default never reaches the line. Fix: route both entry points through one helper that reads isDefaultSelling. Source: SA-580c, board #2554 comment 5893305224.

title: mobile driver adjust.tsx handleScanned hand-rolls +1 box; route it through the scan-level resolver (SA-580)
symptom: handleScanned in the driver at-stop adjust screen adds a scanned product by hand: for a boxed product it does boxes + 1 and recomputes qty as boxes * unitsPerBox + pieces, otherwise qty + 1. It never asks which level the scanned code belongs to, so a code that identifies a unit or a pallet still adds a box. The scan rule (SA-580) resolves the level from the scanned code; this handler should call that scan-level resolver instead of its own arithmetic. Follow-up to SA-595. Source: SA-595c, board #2554 comment 5896990545.

title: lint:migrations flags SET LOCAL without a BEGIN but does not REQUIRE the SA-582 wrap on new migrations, so an unwrapped migration passes
symptom: B896 made lint:migrations refuse a top-level SET LOCAL that sits outside an explicit BEGIN/COMMIT. It only checks placement, so a migration with no SET LOCAL at all passes even though SA-582 requires every new migration to open with the wrap (BEGIN; SET LOCAL lock_timeout; ...; COMMIT;). #2765's unwrapped migration passed lint for that reason. Fix: in diff mode, require the wrap on every NEW migration in the --base range (a file not in the applied-exempt table, matched by folder name and sha256), and fail with <file>: missing SA-582 BEGIN/lock_timeout wrap. Source: board #2554 comment 5897342138 (the #2765 review). Tooling; touches migration checks, plan-only for agents.

title: telescope priceMatchedChunk over prior returns (half-cent per-slice drift, allowed by SA-576)
symptom: priceMatchedChunk prices each returned slice independently, so a line returned in several slices can drift by up to half a cent per slice against pricing the whole quantity once. SA-576 allows the drift for now. Follow-up: telescope the chunk over the prior returns of the line (price the cumulative quantity, subtract what earlier returns already credited), the same shape as the invoice telescope, so slices sum exactly to the whole. Money-adjacent; test tenants only. Source: SA-576a, board #2554 comment 5897475530.

title: google-oauth.service logs the user's email address at two sites (:344 account linked, :730 BuyerAccount created)
symptom: Two log lines write a person's email address to the application log: line 344 logs `Google account linked for user <id> (<email>)` and line 730 logs `BuyerAccount created via Google: <profile.email>`. An email is personal data and does not belong in logs that are shipped and retained. Fix: log ids only (user id, buyer account id), never the email, and pin it with a Logger-spy spec that fails if either message contains the address. Also tracked in ticket #2775. Privacy. Source: board #2554 comment 5901178812.

title: dev-pipeline engine: scope guard reverts test files under a new dir; blocked deps still run; Haiku step committed code
symptom: Run wf_ff1b94ee-b27 (control-system, 2026-09-30): every test-author stage was blocked as 'touched non-test files: apps/control/' because scopeCheckPrompt ran git status --porcelain without --untracked-files=all (a new dir collapses to one ?? entry), and the remediation reverted the authored tests. The wave loop then ran UI1 although its dependency WP7 was blocked, and a Haiku mechanical step (fix-base:UI1:r4) created and committed a 12-file scaffold (preserved as local tag ctl-haiku-backup, reset off the branch).

title: Product row-lock order differs between catalog writers and stock writers: concurrent writes can deadlock (40P01) and return a 500
symptom: PO receive and vendor-bill receive/revert/void lock Product rows id-sorted (component C, lower id, then wants recipe R) while recipe and catalog writers hold R and want C (house order FAMILY row, recipe row, then targets): a lock cycle. Postgres aborts one side with 40P01; bill void/revert and PO receive do not retry, so the user gets a 500. Pre-existing, not a #2803 regression; no data corruption. Fix: one house order, either (A) stock paths lock family/recipe rows first or (B) catalog writers take FOR SHARE on rows they only read. Proof: a real-Postgres two-connection harness, no 40P01 in 20 runs. Source: SA-607b (#2554 5918396805); full body in .claude/sa/TICKET-catalog-lock-order.md. Tier 1, concurrency.

title: Sentinel-guard spec touches the network on red: mock the resend module so it stays hermetic
symptom: The red-first spec "sendSetPasswordEmail to a sentinel is refused too" proves red on unguarded code by letting sendPlatform reach the real Resend client (a network attempt in a unit test). Mock the "resend" module in this spec so the red path is hermetic and cannot hang or flake. Follow-up named by the Opus r2 PASS review of PR #2854 (sentinel-email sweep).

title: isInternalEmail misses display-name recipients: no trim and no "Name <x@sentinel>" parsing
symptom: The helper only string-matches a bare address domain suffix. A recipient such as "Acme Store <acme_store@imported.local>" or one with trailing whitespace passes the guard and reaches a transport. Fix: extract the addr-spec (or trim and parse) before the suffix check, and mirror it in web lib/formatting.ts and mobile lib/internal-email.ts (triple mirror plus the new displayEmail render gate). Follow-up named by the Opus r2 PASS review of PR #2854.

title: sendPlatform logs full recipient addresses: the domain-only rule covers only the sentinel refusal
symptom: The sentinel refusal now logs domain-only (Opus r2 rule: never a full address in logs), but the ordinary success and failure log lines in sendPlatform still print params.to in full. Apply the same domain-only (or masked) convention to those lines. Follow-up named by the Opus r2 PASS review of PR #2854.

title: B285 spec cleanup uses billId instead of vendorBillId and leaks tenants
symptom: The afterAll cleanup deletes by a non-existent billId column instead of vendorBillId, so the cleanup fails or skips and leaks the throwaway tenants. Fixed inside #2803 (check-types ratchet trip on the spec typo). Filed by U-po.

title: VendorBills update() and delete() check DRAFT outside the transaction and take locks in the inverse order
symptom: update() and delete() assert the DRAFT state outside the tx and lock in the inverse order to the receipt paths, so a concurrent receive/void can interleave with them. Fix: call lockBillAndAssertReceiptState first. Fix in flight (U-po). Money-adjacent, medium-high.

title: Bill receipt fingerprint omits totalPaid: a void with credit draws can overwrite a concurrent payment
symptom: The receipt fingerprint does not include totalPaid, so a void with credit draws can overwrite a payment recorded concurrently. Fix: compare totalPaid in the fingerprint or re-read it inside the transaction. Fix in flight (U-po). Money, medium-high.

title: Vendor bill 409 responses carry no machine-readable code
symptom: The bill state-changed and void 409s have no error code, so clients cannot branch on them. Add BILL_STATE_CHANGED and BILL_VOID (api-error-codes plus the types mirror). Fix in flight (U-po).

title: B285 race spec cases (f) and (g) do not assert a lock wait
symptom: Cases (f) and (g) do not assert that a lock wait actually happened, so they could pass without exercising the race. Add the sawLockWait assertion used by case (a). Filed by U-po.

title: Customer dashboard shows "Could not load recent orders." on a fresh e2e tenant
location: apps/web customer dashboard (seen on the e2e-routeflow tenant in the #2794 captures)
symptom: The recent-orders card renders a load error in the capture fixture. Find the failing endpoint or fixture and give the card a readable empty or error state. Pre-existing UI bug found by U-po during the #2794 captures.

title: Driver nav shows two items active at once
symptom: Two driver nav items render as active at the same time (prefix match). Use exact or longest-prefix matching. Pre-existing UI bug found by U-po during the #2794 captures.

title: Inventory and dashboard pages clip the tabs, toolbar, row actions and status at 390 and 768 widths
symptom: At 390 and 768 px the tabs, toolbar, row actions and status column are clipped. Fix: overflow-x wrappers and a responsive toolbar, proved with Playwright at 1440/768/390. Pre-existing UI bug found by U-po during the #2794 captures.

title: Buyer oversell check is per line, not per product
symptom: A buyer order with two lines of the same product, each at or below available stock but whose SUM exceeds available, passes the per-line check and oversells; lines[] can also list the product twice. Fix: aggregate the requested qty per productId before comparing to available, with a DB spec (two lines of 3 vs available 5 must return 409). Owner: U-po after #2871. Found in the #2871 review. Stock, medium-high.

title: Credit-note Apply error toast renders the raw server message (owner rule: no raw server strings)
symptom: POST /credit-notes/:id/apply returns uncoded 400s ("Credit note has expired", "not available for application", "different customers", duplicate selection) via BadRequestException(string), and web handleApply shows err.response.data.message as-is (mobile now shows a generic line). Fix plan: extend the closed CREDIT_NOTE_* set (api-error-codes.ts, packages/types/api/error-codes.ts, mobile stub, #2163 parity) with CREDIT_NOTE_NOT_APPLICABLE, CREDIT_NOTE_EXPIRED, CREDIT_NOTE_CUSTOMER_MISMATCH, CREDIT_NOTE_ALREADY_SELECTED; throw via cnBad() (credit-note-errors.ts); add fixed copy to web and mobile CREDIT_NOTE_ERROR_COPY (parity spec pins equal); replace both Apply onError handlers with creditNoteErrorCopy. Tier 1 (money path), no schema. Family: #2400 / #2418; U1 PR #2867 flags it. Filed via the MacBook lane.

title: seed-marketing-screenshot-products.js fails on InvoiceItem_tenantId_nn
symptom: Running the script against a fresh DB violates the NOT NULL on InvoiceItem.tenantId because the seed writes invoice items without tenantId. Fix: set tenantId on every InvoiceItem write, keeping the test-tenant guard. Pre-existing, found by F2. Tooling, owner unassigned.

title: Mobile api-client queues every failed mutation offline by default, so admin and money writes replay silently after the UI reports failure
symptom: A failed offline save of a setting or money action shows "failed" to the user but replays on reconnect. Seen three times: credit notes (#2867), settings (#2868), REG-B308. Fix: flip the default so only an explicit allow-list of offline-safe endpoints (driver POD and stop updates etc.) may queue and everything else is online-only, plus a static test that any newly queued endpoint must be on the list. Systemic. Owner: N-kit after its web bug PR.

title: dev-pipeline preflight overwrites <runDir>/RESUME.md, erasing human notes
location: tooling · ~/.claude/skills/dev-pipeline/pipeline.js (preflight card writer; out-of-repo engine, canonical copy on ops/engine-sync-2026-09-30)
symptom: The preflight agent writes its own RESUME.md card unconditionally, wiping lane notes and steps already there (it erased a run history and engine-sync steps; restored in LANE-NOTES.md). Suggested fix: write RESUME.md only if absent, or write to RESUME-engine.md. Filed from the docs session via Mac Lead.

title: products clearAll holds one advisory lock per code for the whole catalog in ONE transaction, so a large catalog can exhaust the Postgres shared lock table
symptom: One pg_advisory_xact_lock per barcode code is held for the whole catalog in a single transaction. "out of shared memory" at max_locks_per_transaction x connections (6,400 at the defaults) fails the call and can fail other tenants transactions. After #2860 fold (b) the >1,000-code cap refuses it; this ticket makes large clears possible. Fix: a chunked clearAll with at most 200 products per tx, each with its own sorted code-lock set, idempotent on re-run (inactive products skipped), reporting progress; then lift the cap. Pin: a real-Postgres clear of more than 1,000 referenced products completes with no lock-table error. Source: SA-603l (#2554 5919506098).

title: PrismaService.forTenant() returns the unscoped client when there is no tenant context, so tenant-owned queries read across tenants
symptom: With no tenant context (anonymous route, cron, lost ALS, or SUPER_ADMIN where null means both) forTenant() returns the UNSCOPED client, so a tenant-owned query reads across tenants. Proven harm: #2872 staff-email recipients would include every tenant admins. Security, cross-tenant read. Fix is fail-closed: add a context kind (TENANT, SUPER_ADMIN, ANONYMOUS, SYSTEM); forTenant() throws on ANONYMOUS or no context and on a SUPER_ADMIN tenant-owned create with no tenantId; add an explicit forSystem(reason) door with an allow-list spec. Roll out DARK (warn TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING with a stack) for 7 days, then enforce in a separate diff. Source: SA-619 (#2554 5919576056), full plan and caller audit there.

title: EmailService.send() logs full recipient addresses
symptom: B911 made the sendPlatform logs and the sentinel refusal domain-only, but send() own success and failure log lines still print the full address. Fix: route them through the same domain-only helper (logRecipient). Lead-ordered via Mac Lead.

title: Editing a supplier bill lines leaves the OLD lines in place: nested-created VendorBillItem rows have NULL tenantId, so the tenant-scoped deleteMany misses them
symptom: Create a bill with a line of qty 10, edit it to qty 4: the bill carries both lines ("10,4") while totalOwed is computed from the new items only. Nested-created VendorBillItem rows have NULL tenantId, so the tenant-scoped deleteMany misses them. Fix: delete via the parent nested deleteMany (as revertToDraft does) AND stamp tenantId on the nested creates; the SA rules the platform-wide pattern and audits other nested creates. Money. Owner: U-po after #2878.

title: Nested relation creates leave tenant-owned child rows with NULL tenantId, so tenant-scoped child queries miss them (an edited vendor bill keeps its OLD line beside the new one)
location: apps/api/src/prisma/prisma.service.ts (tenant extension stamps only top-level data/createMany); apps/api/src/vendor-bills/vendor-bills.service.ts:521, :1011 (nested createMany without tenantId), ~:978 (tenant-scoped deleteMany misses NULL rows); about 20 more nested-create sites listed in SA-620
symptom: Nested writes (items: create or createMany) leave tenant-owned children with NULL tenantId; tenant-scoped child queries then miss them. Affected children (nullable tenantId): VendorBillItem, InvoiceItem, EstimateItem, OrderItem, OrderTemplateItem, RecurringInvoiceItem, ReturnItem, RouteStop, PurchaseOrderItem, BillPayment. Systemic parent of B928 (the vendor-bill instance). Fix: B1 the tenant extension stamps nested writes via a DMMF walker; B2 parent-scoped child deletes now, starting with vendor-bills update(items); the owner count-only NULL query first; backfill only by owner decision. Money and tenancy. Source: SA-620 (#2554 5920439272), U-po found the instance.

title: Supplier credit balance is read-modify-written without a lock (cross-bill lost update)
symptom: Two bills applying the same supplier credit concurrently both read the old balance and one write is lost, so the credit is over-spent. Fix: lock the SupplierCredit row FOR UPDATE (sorted, after the bill locks) before reading its balance, with a race pin. Money. Found in the #2878 review. Owner: U-po after #2878.

title: dev-pipeline preflight host-contention gate counts idle daemons, so it never launches under multi-lane load
location: tooling · dev-pipeline pipeline.js preflight (canonical on the PC / ops/engine-sync-2026-09-30; vendored .claude/skills/dev-pipeline)
symptom: The preflight aborts when it counts more than 6 build-tool processes, which includes long-lived turbo daemon, docker and tsc --watch processes. At load1 2.3 on 10 cores it counted 8-18 and aborted run 4. Fix: key on load vs cores (for example load1 above 0.9 x ncpu over two samples), exclude idle daemons and watchers, or add a lead-set args.maxBuildProcs. Filed from the docs session via Mac Lead.

title: dev-pipeline closeout.mjs selftest fails on macOS even on clean master (the tmpdir symlink guard rejects /var to /private/var)
symptom: Run the selftest on the Mac mini: the tmpdir symlink guard rejects /var resolving to /private/var. Fix: resolve the tmpdir with fs.realpathSync before the guard compares. Engine; PC canonical plus a docs PR. Owner unassigned.

title: plane-denylist.json secret-key pattern misses Stripe-style live and test keys
symptom: Keys shaped like the live or test Stripe prefixes never match, because the underscore after live or test breaks the character class, so the Plane mirror and any consumer of this denylist let real key-shaped strings through. Repro: new RegExp("(sk|pk)_[A-Za-z0-9]{12,}").test("sk_live_" + "a".repeat(24)) returns false. Fix: (sk|pk|rk)_(?:live_|test_)?[A-Za-z0-9]{12,} plus a whsec_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,} entry, with a spec case for each. Security and tooling. The control-system build adds its own supplemental patterns meanwhile and does not edit the shared file. Filed via the control-system lane.

title: READ_ONLY toast shows raw server data.message in its description
symptom: The READ_ONLY mutation-error toast renders the server data.message verbatim in its description (owner rule: no raw server strings). Fix: map it to fixed copy. Owner: N-kit (raw-strings program).

title: Bulk-delete partial-success toast joins server skipped[].reason verbatim
symptom: The partial-success toast joins the server skipped[].reason strings as-is (owner rule: no raw server strings). Fix: return reason CODES from the API and map them to fixed sentences in the UI. Owner: N-kit (raw-strings program).

title: driver change-requests POST has no server idempotency: an offline replay can create a second PENDING request
location: apps/api driver change-requests POST (follow-up to B923)
symptom: The driver change-requests POST has no server-side idempotency, so an offline replay of a queued mutation can create a second PENDING request. Follow-up to B923 (mobile api-client queues every failed mutation offline by default). Until fixed, entry 7 of the offline allow-list is online-only. Fix: server idempotency (key or natural-key dedupe) on the POST. Filed for N-kit via the lead.

title: pre-push campaign-check fails in every fresh worktree: the B31 proof points at an untracked local file
location: tooling · scripts/campaign/campaign-check.mjs (undischarged-claim check) and the B31 (F12) ledger row pointing at .claude/pipeline/2026-09-06-F12-route-windows/build-plan.md
symptom: git push from a new worktree off master fails pre-push with "1 undischarged claim(s): B31 (F12): build-plan.md not found". The file is not tracked in git (the F12 pipeline directory is empty on origin/master); it exists only in one local checkout. Workaround: copy the directory into the worktree (left untracked). Fix: commit that build-plan.md, or make the T3 build-plan proof point at a tracked path, or tolerate missing local pipeline artifacts with a warning. Tooling, blocks pushes. Filed via the control-system lane.

title: Control system PR #2900: docs tell the owner to run ctl seed and ctl lane register, but neither command exists, so first use is blocked
location: apps/control (PR #2900): src/main.ts seedFixtureOrigin (fixture mode only), the PR body Owner setup steps 3 and 5, the dashboard no-lanes empty state, apps/control/README.md (no runbook)
symptom: The PR body Owner setup steps 3 and 5 and the dashboard empty state tell the owner to run ctl seed and ctl lane register. Neither exists: ctl lane register x exits 2 (unknown subcommand register) and ctl seed exits 2 with the usage text. Nothing creates the orphan ctl/state branch on a real origin (only fixture mode does). Repro: an empty bare repo as CONTROL_STATE_ORIGIN, then ctl next prints UNAVAILABLE clone failed: Remote branch ctl/state not found, and ctl start RF-1 --lane x exits 5 with the event parked in pending/; the server cannot clone it either. Blocks first use; no data risk. Fix: a small follow-up code PR adding ctl init and ctl lane register <id> --name --machine --kind, tests first, plus a README runbook. Filed via the control-system lane.

title: Control system dashboard: the Open pull requests panel, its count and the lane-card PR chip omit PRs in the ready state
location: apps/control/src/render/panels.ts (prsPanel, prFor) vs src/domain/prs.ts:174 (PRState includes ready) and waste.ts isOpen
symptom: The panel, its count and the lane PR chip only include PRs whose state is open or draft, but the domain PRState also has ready (approved, CI green, mergeable clean), which waste.ts isOpen counts. A PR that is ready to merge therefore disappears from the panel, the count and the lane chip: wrong status for exactly the PRs nearest to merging. Repro: a fixture PR with review approved, ci green, mergeable clean renders in none of those. Fix: include ready in both filters, with a test (one line each). Control-system PR #2900; Mac Lead decides whether it lands in #2900 or the stacked plain-language PR. Filed via the control-system lane.

title: janitor:apply crashes on a stray file: safeRemoveTree runs rmdir /s /q on a FILE and aborts before the Docker and npm-cache steps (win32)
symptom: safeRemoveTree runs rmdir /s /q on a plain FILE (for example a stray bugs-selftest.log), which fails on win32 and aborts janitor:apply before the Docker and npm-cache reclaim steps. Fix: stat the target and use unlink (or fs.rm) for a file, rmdir only for a directory, and keep the safety checks. Tooling. Found during the PC cleanup. Filed via the lead.

title: Control system PR #2900: the 200-concurrent-uploads memory probe is order-dependent and can false-red every PR Verify once merged
location: apps/control/test/wp7-security.spec.ts (test 5b: 200 concurrent fake-signature 1 MB uploads grow memory < 50 MB; a signed delivery still works)
symptom: The probe measures in-process heapUsed plus arrayBuffers growth against a 50 MB bound with no warm-up, so the result depends on test order and heap state. It passes inside the whole-file run, but run alone (jest -t "200 concurrent") it fails 6 of 6 with 78-89 MB growth, and it failed once under load in the pre-push verify (turbo, @routeflow/control#test) before passing on the rerun. Once #2900 merges it can false-red every PR Verify. Fix plan: a tests-only commit on stacked PR #2905 that makes the probe order-independent (warm-up flood, then measure) and still goes red on a deliberately buffered 200 MB body. Filed via the control-system lane.

title: linkAppleAccount still refuses a null Apple email with 403 although linking does not need it
location: apps/api auth Apple service linkAppleAccount (follow-up to #2486 / PR #2910)
symptom: Apple sends the email claim only on the first sign-in. linkAppleAccount still refuses a null email with 403 even though linking by sub does not need the email. Not folded into #2910; separate ticket from the Opus self-review. Fix: allow the link when the token carries a verified sub and the user is authenticated, without requiring an email. Filed via Mac Lead from the #2910 body.

title: buyer-merge googleId transfer writes the primary before nulling the secondary while googleId is unique
location: apps/api buyer-merge.service.ts googleId transfer (pre-existing; PR #2910 body item)
symptom: The googleId transfer writes the primary before nulling the secondary while BuyerAccount googleId is @unique, so the write can hit the unique index (P2002). Pre-existing. Fix: mirror the new appleId ordering from #2910 (clear the secondary first, then inherit on the primary), with a DB spec. Not folded into #2910; filed via Mac Lead.

title: Secondary buyer Apple refresh token is discarded without an Apple revoke when the primary already has an appleId
symptom: When the primary already has an appleId, the secondary Apple refresh token is discarded without calling Apple /auth/revoke, leaving a live Apple grant for an account that no longer exists. Fix: revoke the secondary token at Apple during the merge (best effort, logged). Not folded into #2910; filed via Mac Lead.

title: Two older mobile settings writes can still be offline-queued and replay later (REG-B308 class)
symptom: The mobile api-client queues failed-offline mutations unless the request passes _skipOfflineQueue: true. #2868 opts its three new admin writes out via lib/api/settings-parity.ts, but the General tab business-settings save and the push-notifications preference write on the same Settings screen still enter the queue: the UI shows a "Couldn t save" toast offline, then the change silently applies later when the queue replays. Fix: pass { _skipOfflineQueue: true } on both PATCHes (same pattern as settings-parity.ts) with a mock-apiClient test per call (see apps/mobile/__tests__/settings-parity-api.test.ts). Same class as B923. Found in the Opus self-review of #2868; filed via Lane B.

title: A credit note plus a return refund on the same invoice line can credit more than the line value (multi-line invoices)
location: apps/api/src/returns/returns.service.ts (processRefund, ~:596 billedBasisFor, :663 invoice-headroom check); apps/api/src/credit-notes/credit-notes.service.ts (create per-line cap ~:165-198)
symptom: On a two-line $200 invoice (line A $100), a credit note of $33.33 (3 units) followed by a return of all 10 units refunded at $100 credits line A $133.33; both writes are accepted (201). Single-line invoices are blocked only by the invoice-level headroom check. Cause: ReturnsService.processRefund mints a lump-sum credit note with no items (amount from billedBasisFor) and checks only the invoice headroom; CreditNotesService.create's per-line cap counts only item-bearing credit notes, and the returns cap does not subtract prior credit-note credits. Found by the F2 proof on master d486363d (#2554 comment 5926574557). Money, tier-1.

title: Return refund on a 2+-invoice order is headroom-checked against the latest invoice's lines only
location: apps/api/src/returns/returns.service.ts (processRefund / billedBasisFor / itemiseRefund; lump-sum credit note on the latest invoice); apps/api/src/credit-notes/line-credit-headroom.ts (allocateProductQty, loadLineCredits)
symptom: Follow-up of B946 (SA-628a, #2554 5927765098). For an order with 2+ creditable invoices the refund keeps a lump-sum credit note, bounded only by the order-wide and latest-invoice headroom, so goods billed on an earlier invoice can be credited past that invoice's line value. Return.creditNoteId is a single link, so full itemisation across invoices needs a schema change (Sitting C). No-migration interim fix: run the same refund-mode line-headroom check (allocateProductQty mode refund, using each invoice's loadLineCredits, oldest first) across ALL creditable invoices; a shortfall is the 409; the mint stays one lump-sum CN. Money, tier-1.

title: Inline-return standalone credit notes are not counted in line credit headroom (a second over-credit path)
symptom: Follow-up of B946 (SA-628a, #2554 5927765098). Inline-return standalone credit notes carry no invoiceId, so loadLineCredits never counts them; a credit note on a line plus an inline return of the same goods can credit more than the line value. Inline ReturnItem rows snapshot sourceInvoiceItemId, subtotal and qty, so they are attributable without a migration. Fix: add an inline term to loadLineCredits (sum of ReturnItem credit for sourceInvoiceItemId in the lines whose credit is not VOID) and have the inline pricer check the same helper in refund mode before minting. F2 probes first (a CN on a line plus an inline return of the same goods). Money, tier-1.

title: voidInvoice can restore an application of a SOURCE_DELETED credit note to spendable (orphan credit)

Fix shape (SA): refuse with 409 CREDIT_NOTE_SOURCE_GONE when voidInvoice would reverse an application of a SOURCE_DELETED note, never restore it; plus a count-only sizing query (read-only, per SA post). title: Control security spec: the 200 concurrent fake-signature 1 MB uploads test fails deterministically on macOS (EPIPE/ECONNRESET counted as 0, not rejected)
location: apps/control/test/wp7-security.spec.ts (test: 200 concurrent fake-signature 1 MB uploads all get 401, and a signed delivery still works)
symptom: Reported by the documentation alignment review lane via Mac Lead. From #2900/#2905 on master the test fails DETERMINISTICALLY on the MacBook (macOS) and passes on Linux and the Mac mini: some raw-socket POSTs resolve 0 because the client socket errors (EPIPE/ECONNRESET) while it keeps writing 1 MB after the server has already rejected and closed, and the test maps any socket error to 0 and asserts every code is 401. Fix plan: tests-only PR off master: a reset after the server's rejection counts as rejected, proven by a server-side spy that every response the server sent was a 401 and none was accepted; keep the memory-bound test; mutation-proven, red-first on a forced EPIPE.

symptom: From SA-606s (#2554 5945656748), via Mac Lead; pre-existing on master; VERIFIED BY READING master's buyer.controller.ts (not executed).
